options: The RADIUS server used for network logins is not reachable
Kerberos tickets are rejected when clocks differ beyond the allowed skew
All user passwords have expired globally on the same day
The ticket-granting ticket has been encrypted with a weak cipher
questions.explanation: Kerberos depends on synchronized time, with a default tolerance of about five minutes, so a large skew causes ticket validation to fail. A weak cipher would not produce a clean time-related failure, expired passwords would affect other services too, and RADIUS is not part of Kerberos authentication.

questions.question: A network team needs per-command authorization and full payload encryption for administrators logging into routers and switches. Which protocol suits this requirement BEST?
options: TACACS+
SNMPv2c
Telnet with a login banner
RADIUS
questions.explanation: TACACS+ separates authentication, authorization and accounting, supports per-command authorization and encrypts the whole payload. RADIUS combines authentication and authorization and encrypts only the password. SNMPv2c is a monitoring protocol with cleartext community strings, and Telnet is unencrypted.

questions.question: A government agency requires that file access be determined by sensitivity labels assigned by a security officer, and that file owners cannot grant exceptions. Which access control model is this?
options: Mandatory access control
Discretionary access control
Role-based access control
Rule-based access control using firewalls
questions.explanation: In MAC a central authority assigns labels and the system enforces them, and owners cannot override them. Under DAC owners decide who gets access. RBAC grants rights by job role, and rule-based control applies fixed rules unrelated to central labels.

questions.question: A company wants access decisions that consider the user's department, the device's patch status, the data's classification tag and the time of day. Which model fits BEST?
options: Access control lists on individual files
Static role-based access control
Discretionary access control
Attribute-based access control
questions.explanation: ABAC evaluates multiple attributes of the subject, resource and environment at request time. DAC depends on owner-defined permissions. Static RBAC uses job role alone, and file ACLs cannot express device health or time-of-day conditions dynamically.

questions.question: An employee transfers from finance to marketing. Six months later an access review shows she still has the finance application roles and the marketing roles. What process failure does this illustrate?
options: Normal and expected behaviour for a properly run role-based system
Cryptographic key compromise of the finance application
Privilege creep from missing access recertification and role-change deprovisioning
A failure of the data retention schedule for finance records
questions.explanation: Accumulating rights as roles change is privilege creep, and it should be removed by role-change processes and periodic access reviews. Data retention is unrelated, nothing suggests a key compromise, and RBAC is designed to prevent, not allow, unneeded rights.

questions.question: A privileged administrator is dismissed for misconduct at noon. What should happen FIRST?
options: Reset the password and give it to the manager so work can continue
Wait until the end of the working day to avoid disrupting the team, then disable the account quietly
Delete the account and all its files to remove any trace of access
Disable the account and revoke access immediately, preserving the account for investigation
questions.explanation: Access must be removed immediately, and disabling instead of deleting preserves evidence and mailbox data. Deletion destroys evidence, waiting leaves a window for sabotage, and handing the credentials to a manager breaks accountability and gives another person a shared secret.

questions.question: An application uses a service account whose password has not changed in six years and is hard-coded in several scripts. Which remediation is BEST?
options: Add the account to the Domain Admins group so scripts do not fail
Keep the password the same but remove it from all documentation
Disable account lockout for the service account so scripts never fail
Move to a managed identity or vaulted, rotated secret with least-privilege permissions
questions.explanation: Non-human credentials should be vaulted or replaced by managed identities, rotated automatically and limited to what the task needs. Adding administrative rights worsens the exposure, hiding the documentation does not change the exposure, and disabling lockout removes a protection.

questions.question: A server hosts a critical application and has a known unpatched vulnerability. No known exploit exists and the server is isolated on a network with no inbound or outbound internet access. Which statement BEST describes the risk?
options: Risk is reduced because both threat likelihood and exposure are low
Risk is maximal because the vulnerability exists on a critical server
There is no risk at all because no public exploit exists yet
Risk cannot be assessed at all without first obtaining a CVSS score
questions.explanation: Risk combines likelihood and impact, and isolation plus no known exploit lowers likelihood even though the asset is valuable. A vulnerability alone does not make risk maximal, and risk is not zero just because no exploit is known today. CVSS describes severity but is not required to reason about risk.

questions.question: A company decides to stop offering a service in a region because compliance costs would exceed profits. Which risk treatment is this?
options: Transference
Avoidance
Acceptance
Mitigation
questions.explanation: Stopping the activity that generates the risk is avoidance. Transference shifts the financial impact to another party such as an insurer. Mitigation adds controls to reduce risk, and acceptance means continuing while tolerating it.

questions.question: A server worth 200,000 dollars would lose 25 percent of its value in a flood. Floods are expected once every five years. What is the annualized loss expectancy?
options: 40,000 dollars
250,000 dollars
50,000 dollars
10,000 dollars
questions.explanation: SLE is 200,000 times 0.25, or 50,000 dollars. The ARO is one event in five years, or 0.2 per year, so the ALE is 50,000 times 0.2, or 10,000 dollars. The 50,000 figure is only the single loss expectancy, and the other values do not follow from the formula.

questions.question: A control costs 18,000 dollars per year and reduces the ALE of a risk from 40,000 to 12,000 dollars. What should the risk manager conclude?
options: It is not justified because it costs more than the residual ALE
It is not justified because the residual ALE is still above zero
It cannot be evaluated until a qualitative risk scoring exercise is completed
It is cost-justified because the 28,000 reduction exceeds its cost
questions.explanation: A control is worthwhile when the reduction in expected loss exceeds its cost, and 28,000 is greater than 18,000. Residual risk above zero is expected and does not make a control worthless. Comparing cost to the residual ALE is the wrong test, and the quantitative figures are enough to decide.

questions.question: After applying controls, management formally accepts a small remaining chance of a short outage. What is the remaining risk called?
options: Residual risk remaining after the hardening controls were applied
Inherent risk
Transferred risk
Aggregate risk
questions.explanation: Residual risk is what remains after controls. Inherent risk is the level before controls are considered. Transferred risk has been shifted elsewhere rather than remaining, and aggregate risk refers to the combined total of many risks.

questions.question: A vulnerability scanner reports missing patches on a database server. The security team suspects many findings are false positives because the scan was unauthenticated. What action BEST improves accuracy?
options: Run a credentialed scan against the server
Run the same unauthenticated scan more often during the week
Ignore every finding rated below critical severity
Disable the scanner's vulnerability checks
questions.explanation: Credentialed scans inspect patch levels and configuration from inside the system, which reduces both false positives and negatives. Disabling checks removes coverage, ignoring lower severities discards real issues, and repeating the same unauthenticated scan reproduces the same inaccuracy.

questions.question: Two vulnerabilities each score CVSS 9.8. One is on an internet-facing server holding customer data and is being exploited in the wild. The other is on an isolated lab machine with no sensitive data. How should remediation be prioritized?
options: Patch both in the same maintenance window because the CVSS scores are equal and so the risk must be equal
Defer both until the next scheduled maintenance cycle to reduce disruption
Patch the lab machine first because the change is easier to make
Patch the internet-facing server first, because exposure and active exploitation raise its risk
questions.explanation: CVSS measures technical severity, and prioritization should consider exposure, active exploitation and asset criticality. Treating equal scores as equal risk ignores context. Ease of fixing is not a priority criterion on its own, and deferring an actively exploited internet-facing flaw is poor practice.

questions.question: A tester is hired to assess a company's web application. The testers are given a standard user account and the architecture diagram but no source code. What type of test is this?
options: White box
Black box
Gray box
Blind red team
questions.explanation: Partial knowledge such as an account and diagram is gray box. Black box means no prior knowledge, and white box provides full details including source code. A blind red team exercise is a different, objective-driven engagement.

questions.question: A security consultant is asked to start a penetration test of the production network next week. The scope, contacts and testing windows have not been agreed. What is the MOST appropriate next step?
options: Begin passive reconnaissance now to save time once approval arrives
Obtain written authorization and agree rules of engagement before any testing
Start with a low-impact scan and seek formal approval afterwards
Ask the system administrators to approve the test verbally
questions.explanation: Testing requires explicit written authorization from someone entitled to give it, along with agreed scope and rules. Starting reconnaissance or scanning first can be unauthorized access, and a verbal approval from administrators does not constitute proper authority or documentation.

questions.question: A SIEM analyst notices that logon events from two servers appear several minutes out of order, making a timeline of an attack unreliable. What is the MOST likely root cause and fix?
options: Weak passwords on the servers; enforce stricter complexity rules
Missing antivirus software; install agents on every server
Insufficient disk space on the SIEM; add more storage
Unsynchronized clocks; configure NTP on all sources
questions.explanation: Event correlation depends on consistent time, so unsynchronized clocks distort timelines and are fixed by NTP. Storage, antivirus and password policy do not explain timestamps that are out of order.

questions.question: A network IDS built on signatures has failed to alert on a brand-new attack technique that no vendor has published rules for. Which detection approach would be MOST likely to catch it?
options: A host-based firewall rule blocking the attacker's address
More frequent signature updates from the vendor only
Increasing the log retention period for the sensors
Anomaly or behaviour-based detection against a baseline
questions.explanation: Behaviour-based methods look for deviations from normal and can flag unknown attacks, at the cost of more false positives. Signatures cannot match patterns they have never seen, a firewall rule is not detection, and retention length does not change what is detected.

questions.question: An analyst reviews a business impact analysis. Which finding would MOST directly determine how often a payments database must be replicated to a recovery site?
options: The operating system version running on the database server
The firewall vendor in use at the recovery site
The recovery point objective for the payments function
The number of administrators with access to the database
questions.explanation: The RPO is the maximum tolerable data loss, which sets replication or backup frequency. The administrator count, firewall vendor and operating system version affect other decisions but not how much data may be lost.

questions.question: A security team wants a metric that shows leadership whether detection is improving over time. Which is the MOST meaningful?
options: Total number of firewall rules
Total gigabytes of logs stored
Mean time to detect incidents
Number of employees attending lunch-and-learns
questions.explanation: Mean time to detect measures outcome and trends toward faster discovery. Rule counts, attendance and log volume are activity measures that do not show whether detection is effective.

questions.question: A SOC analyst confirms that a workstation is beaconing to a known command-and-control address. According to a standard incident response lifecycle, which action belongs to the containment phase?
options: Writing the lessons-learned report for senior management
Rebuilding the workstation from a known-clean image
Isolating the workstation from the network while preserving its state
Updating the incident response plan with the new findings
questions.explanation: Isolation limits spread and keeps volatile evidence, which is containment. Rebuilding from a clean image is eradication and recovery, and the lessons-learned report and plan updates belong to the post-incident phase.

questions.question: An analyst discovers a compromised server running a suspicious process. What should be done FIRST to preserve the most volatile evidence?
options: Run a full antivirus scan and delete anything it flags
Reinstall the operating system to remove the attacker's access
Capture memory and active network connections before any shutdown
Power off the server immediately to stop the attacker
questions.explanation: Volatile data such as memory, processes and connections is lost at power-off, so it is captured first as the order of volatility dictates. Powering off, scanning and deleting, or reinstalling all destroy evidence before it is collected.

questions.question: A forensic examiner needs to analyze a suspect laptop's drive for use in court. Which procedure is MOST appropriate?
options: Attach it to a write blocker, create a hashed bit-for-bit image and analyze the copy
Ask the user to export their documents to a shared drive
Boot the laptop and copy the relevant files to a USB stick, noting the time of each copy in a log
Run file recovery tools directly on the original drive
questions.explanation: A write blocker prevents changes, and a hash-verified image lets the examiner prove the analysis copy matches the original. Booting or running tools on the original alters it, and user-supplied exports are incomplete and untrustworthy as evidence.

questions.question: During an investigation, a laptop was passed from the helpdesk to a manager and then to the forensic lab with no paperwork. What is the MOST likely consequence?
options: The evidence may be challenged or excluded because custody cannot be demonstrated
The hash value of the drive changes each time it is handed over
Nothing at all, because digital evidence can never be altered
The evidence becomes stronger because fewer people handled it
questions.explanation: Undocumented handling breaks the chain of custody, which undermines the claim that the evidence is authentic. Fewer handlers do not help if the transfers are undocumented, handling does not change a hash by itself, and digital evidence can absolutely be altered.

questions.question: An incident handler restores a file server from last night's backup after a malware infection. Two days later the malware reappears. Which step was MOST likely skipped?
options: Changing the server's hostname and IP address after the restore
Notifying the press before restoring any service
Documenting the post-incident review before the restore began
Verifying the backup was clean and eradicating the root cause and persistence
questions.explanation: Restoring without confirming that the backup predates the compromise or removing the persistence mechanism and entry point reintroduces the problem. Press notification, documentation and a new hostname do not prevent reinfection.

questions.question: A business function has a maximum tolerable downtime of 8 hours. The disaster recovery team proposes a recovery method that takes 10 hours to bring the system up. What is the problem?
options: The recovery time objective exceeds the maximum tolerable downtime
The recovery point objective is longer than the maximum tolerable downtime
The backups are not differential, so restoring takes longer
The plan lacks a warm site, which every recovery plan requires
questions.explanation: The RTO must be shorter than the MTD, otherwise the business suffers unacceptable harm before recovery. RPO concerns data loss rather than time to restore, backup type is not indicated as the cause, and the site type is a means, not the requirement that is violated.

questions.question: A retailer needs to restore its order system within 4 hours with no more than 15 minutes of lost transactions, at the lowest cost that meets the requirement. Which arrangement BEST fits?
options: A hot site with duplicate hardware idling at all times
A reciprocal agreement with a competitor
A cold site with weekly backups held in the same building
A warm site with continuous replication and a few hours of setup time
questions.explanation: Continuous replication satisfies the 15-minute RPO, and a few hours of setup fits within the 4-hour RTO at lower cost than a hot site. A cold site and weekly backups cannot meet either target, a reciprocal agreement is unreliable, and the hot site would exceed the requirement and the budget.

questions.question: A file server is backed up with a full backup on Sunday and incremental backups Monday to Thursday. It fails on Friday morning. Which backups are needed to restore it?
options: Only Sunday's full backup
Sunday's full backup and all four incrementals
Only Thursday's incremental
Sunday's full backup and Thursday's incremental only
questions.explanation: Incrementals capture only changes since the previous backup, so the restore needs the full backup plus every incremental in order. Using only the latest incremental or skipping some leaves out data. A differential strategy would need only the full and the latest differential.

questions.question: A company wants to test its disaster recovery plan by switching real processing to the alternate site while the primary site continues running, so that results can be compared without risk to operations. Which test is this?
options: Tabletop exercise
Full interruption test
Parallel test
Read-through
questions.explanation: A parallel test brings up recovery systems and runs them alongside production. A tabletop is a discussion, a full interruption halts production and fails over for real, and a read-through only reviews the plan's content.

questions.question: Ransomware has encrypted several file servers, and the backup server is reachable from the same domain. What is the BEST containment action?
options: Isolate affected systems from the network and protect or disconnect backup repositories
Pay the ransom immediately to restore operations as quickly as possible, then investigate afterwards
Delete the encrypted files so the malware cannot spread further
Reboot all servers at once to clear the malware from memory
questions.explanation: Isolation stops spread, and protecting backups preserves the recovery path from attackers who target them. Paying is a business and legal decision with no guarantee and is not containment, rebooting can destroy evidence and does not remove the malware, and deleting files destroys data.

questions.question: Who should authorize communications about a data breach to customers and regulators?
options: Any analyst who handled the incident, because that person understands the technical details best
The system administrator who runs the affected server
The attacker, through negotiation over what is disclosed
Designated spokespeople and management following the communication plan, with legal review
questions.explanation: External communications are controlled, consistent and reviewed by legal so statements are accurate and meet notification laws. Individual analysts or administrators speaking independently risk inconsistent or damaging messages, and the attacker plays no role.

questions.question: A company is notified of a lawsuit related to a past project. The email server automatically deletes messages after 90 days. What should the organization do FIRST?
options: Move the mailboxes to a personal account
Issue a legal hold and suspend automatic deletion for relevant data
Delete the relevant mailboxes to limit exposure
Continue normal deletion to follow the retention policy, since the lawsuit has not been decided yet
questions.explanation: A legal hold preserves potentially relevant information and suspends routine destruction. Continuing deletion or deliberately deleting mailboxes can be spoliation, and moving data to personal accounts loses control of it.

questions.question: After a major incident is closed, the CSIRT meets to discuss what detection gaps allowed the attacker to stay undetected for weeks and updates its monitoring rules. Which phase is this?
options: Post-incident activity
Containment
Preparation
Eradication
questions.explanation: Reviewing what happened and improving controls afterwards is post-incident activity. Preparation happens before incidents, though findings feed back into it. Eradication removes the threat and containment limits its spread.

questions.question: A company needs to encrypt a 500 GB backup quickly and also securely send the encryption key to a remote office. Which combination is MOST appropriate?
options: RSA for the bulk data and AES to send the key to the remote office, because RSA is the faster of the two
AES for the data and a hash of the key sent in cleartext
SHA-256 for the data and RSA for the key
AES for the data and the remote office's RSA public key to protect the AES key
questions.explanation: Hybrid cryptography uses fast symmetric encryption for bulk data and asymmetric encryption to protect the symmetric key. Using RSA for bulk data is impractical, hashing is not encryption, and sending key material in cleartext defeats the purpose.

questions.question: Alice wants to send Bob a confidential message that only Bob can read. Which key should Alice use to encrypt it?
options: Alice's public key
Alice's private key
Bob's private key
Bob's public key
questions.explanation: Encrypting with the recipient's public key means only the holder of the matching private key can decrypt. Alice's private key would produce a signature, which anyone can verify, so there is no confidentiality. Alice's public key would not let Bob decrypt, and Alice does not have Bob's private key.

questions.question: Which property does a digital signature provide that an HMAC does NOT?
options: Authentication of the origin to the receiver
Integrity
Use of a hash function
Non-repudiation
questions.explanation: Because the signer's private key is unique to them, a signature proves who signed and the signer cannot credibly deny it. An HMAC uses a shared secret that both sides know, so either could have produced it. Integrity and origin authentication are provided by both, and both use hashes.

questions.question: A security reviewer finds that an application encrypts database records with AES in ECB mode and flags it. What is the PRIMARY concern?
options: Identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks, revealing patterns
ECB mode is too slow to be practical for large databases, since each block is processed one by one
ECB mode does not support 256-bit AES keys at all
ECB mode effectively makes the encryption key shorter
questions.explanation: ECB encrypts each block independently so repeated plaintext patterns remain visible. Mode choice does not shorten keys, ECB is not especially slow, and it works with any AES key size. An authenticated mode such as GCM is the better choice.

questions.question: A certificate authority's private key may have been exposed in a breach. What is the MOST appropriate response?
options: Wait until the issued certificates expire naturally and then reissue them from the same exposed key
Revoke the CA's certificate, reissue from a new key and notify relying parties
Shorten the validity period of all newly issued certificates
Change the server passwords only
questions.explanation: Exposure of a CA key undermines trust in everything it signed, so the CA must be revoked and replaced and relying parties informed. Waiting leaves forged certificates trusted, server passwords are unrelated, and shorter validity for new certificates does not address already issued ones.

questions.question: Which statement about TLS 1.3 compared to older versions is correct?
options: It supports RC4 and static RSA key exchange for compatibility with older clients and servers
It encrypts only the application data and not the handshake
It is only used to protect email and nothing else
It requires forward secrecy through ephemeral key exchange and removes legacy ciphers
questions.explanation: TLS 1.3 removed weak algorithms and static RSA key exchange and always uses ephemeral key exchange, giving forward secrecy. It does not support RC4, it encrypts more of the handshake than older versions, and it is used for many protocols beyond email.

questions.question: A security engineer must store a CA's root private key so that it cannot be extracted even by administrators. Which solution is BEST?
options: The root key copied to every issuing server
A password-protected USB stick kept in a locked desk drawer in the security office
A hardware security module in a controlled, offline facility
An encrypted file on a file server
questions.explanation: An HSM generates and uses the key inside a tamper-resistant boundary and never exposes it, and keeping the root offline reduces its attack surface. A file on a server, a stick in a drawer, and copies on every server are all easier to steal.

questions.question: A developer says the application is secure because it hashes user files with SHA-256 and sends the hash along with each file. An attacker who intercepts the traffic modifies a file and recomputes the hash. What was missing?
options: A second hash computed over the first hash value
A keyed construction such as HMAC or a digital signature
A longer hash output such as SHA-512 instead of SHA-256
A faster hash algorithm so recalculation is harder to notice
questions.explanation: An unkeyed hash can be recomputed by anyone, so it protects only against accidental changes. HMAC or a signature requires a secret or private key the attacker lacks. Output length, speed and repeated hashing do not solve the lack of a secret.

questions.question: A user reports that a web page loads on an IP address but not by hostname. At which layer of the OSI model should troubleshooting for name resolution generally begin?
options: Data link layer
Physical layer
Transport layer, because DNS uses TCP only
Application layer, where DNS operates
questions.explanation: DNS is an application-layer service, and the symptom shows that connectivity works but name lookup fails. The physical and data link layers are evidently working. DNS uses UDP for most queries and TCP for some, so it is not exclusively a transport-layer problem.

questions.question: An attacker sends a flood of TCP SYN packets with spoofed source addresses to a web server. The server's connection table fills up. Which mitigation is MOST directly effective?
options: Increase the web server's disk space to hold more connections
Require longer passwords for administrators of the web server
Enable SYN cookies and rate limiting
Disable UDP on the router
questions.explanation: SYN cookies avoid keeping state for half-open connections, and rate limiting slows the flood. Disabling UDP does not affect a TCP attack, disk space is unrelated, and passwords play no role in a handshake flood.

questions.question: A company hosts a public web server, a mail relay and an internal database. Which design BEST limits the damage if the web server is compromised?
options: Use NAT on the web server only and leave the rest unchanged
Place the public servers in a DMZ with firewalls restricting traffic into the internal network
Place the database in the DMZ for faster access
Place all servers on the internal network behind one firewall, because a single firewall is simpler to manage and audit
questions.explanation: A DMZ separates exposed services from internal assets, and firewall rules limit what a compromised server can reach. A single flat network lets an attacker move freely, the database should not be placed in the DMZ, and NAT does not protect against compromise.

questions.question: An auditor finds that an unknown laptop plugged into a wall jack in a conference room immediately received full network access. Which control would have prevented this?
options: A longer DHCP lease time on the conference room VLAN
Changing the default gateway address of the network
Hiding the wireless SSID of the guest network
IEEE 802.1X port-based network access control
questions.explanation: 802.1X requires a device to authenticate before the switch port passes traffic. Hiding an SSID applies to wireless only, DHCP lease length and the gateway address do nothing to stop an unauthorized device connecting.

questions.question: A firewall administrator is reviewing an access list that is processed top to bottom, with the first match applied. Which arrangement is MOST appropriate?
options: Specific permit and deny rules first, then broader rules, ending with an explicit deny all
A permit-all rule first, followed by specific denials
Rules ordered alphabetically by description
A deny-all rule at the top of the list with specific permit rules placed below it for each service
questions.explanation: With first-match processing, specific rules must precede general ones, and a final default deny enforces least privilege. A permit-all rule at the top makes later denials unreachable, alphabetical ordering is meaningless, and a deny-all at the top blocks everything before any permit is evaluated.

questions.question: A remote worker uses a VPN configured with split tunnelling while connected to a hotel network. What is the PRIMARY risk compared with full tunnelling?
options: The VPN will assign the worker's laptop a duplicate IP address that conflicts with the hotel network's gateway
The worker cannot reach any internal resources while connected, because the hotel network blocks VPN traffic
The VPN is unable to encrypt the corporate traffic it carries, because encryption is switched off by split tunnelling
Internet traffic bypasses corporate inspection and the laptop bridges a hostile network and the corporate one
questions.explanation: Split tunnelling leaves the endpoint connected to both the untrusted local network and the corporate network and sends internet traffic outside corporate controls. Corporate traffic is still encrypted, and internal access still works, so those answers describe features that are not impacted.

questions.question: A branch office needs to connect permanently to headquarters over the internet so that all traffic between the two networks is encrypted by the edge gateways. Which IPsec configuration fits?
options: ESP in transport mode with SNMP
ESP in tunnel mode between the gateways
AH in transport mode between each host
No encryption, using only authentication headers
questions.explanation: Gateway-to-gateway VPNs use tunnel mode, and ESP provides confidentiality as well as integrity. AH provides no encryption, and transport mode between every host is not a site-to-site design. SNMP is a monitoring protocol and has no role here.

questions.question: A small business wants to secure its wireless network used by employees and wants individual credentials that can be revoked when someone leaves. Which configuration is BEST?
options: WPA2 Personal with a shared passphrase changed yearly
WPA3 or WPA2 Enterprise with 802.1X and a RADIUS server
An open network with a captive portal and MAC filtering
WEP with a long key and a hidden network name
questions.explanation: Enterprise mode authenticates each user, so access can be revoked individually and activity attributed. A shared passphrase cannot be revoked per person, WEP is broken, and an open network with MAC filtering offers weak protection since MAC addresses are trivially spoofed.

questions.question: An attacker places a device that broadcasts the same SSID as the corporate Wi-Fi in a coffee shop, and employees connect to it automatically. What is this attack?
options: Bluejacking
Evil twin
VLAN hopping
War driving
questions.explanation: A hostile access point that impersonates a legitimate network is an evil twin. Bluejacking sends unsolicited Bluetooth messages, war driving is surveying wireless networks, and VLAN hopping is a switch-level attack.

questions.question: A switch administrator wants to stop attackers on a LAN from poisoning ARP caches to intercept traffic. Which feature should be enabled?
options: Telnet access to the switch for remote management
Port mirroring enabled on every access port
Spanning tree protocol with the root bridge set manually
Dynamic ARP inspection with DHCP snooping
questions.explanation: Dynamic ARP inspection validates ARP messages against trusted bindings learned through DHCP snooping. Spanning tree prevents loops, port mirroring copies traffic to a sensor and helps no one stop poisoning, and Telnet is an insecure management protocol.

questions.question: A security engineer suspects data is being exfiltrated through DNS queries containing long, encoded subdomains sent to an external server. Which control would MOST help detect this?
options: Enabling DHCP reservations for all internal servers
Monitoring DNS query logs for unusual volume and name length
Increasing the firewall's UDP session timeout
Deploying a Type 2 hypervisor on analyst workstations to run suspicious files
questions.explanation: DNS tunnelling shows up as abnormal query patterns, so DNS logging and analysis detect it. Timeouts, DHCP reservations and hypervisor type have nothing to do with identifying that traffic.

questions.question: A company wants to give employees access to specific internal web applications from any location without placing their devices on the corporate network. Which approach BEST aligns with zero trust?
options: A full-tunnel VPN granting access to the entire internal network once the user has logged in
Zero Trust Network Access with per-application authorization and device posture checks
Shared accounts protected by a single long password
Port forwarding all application ports on the perimeter firewall
questions.explanation: ZTNA grants narrow access to each application after verifying user and device. A full-tunnel VPN gives broad network access, which is the implicit trust zero trust avoids. Port forwarding exposes services directly, and shared accounts destroy accountability.

questions.question: A network engineer is told to use SNMP to monitor routers in a way that prevents sniffing of the credentials. Which version should be used?
options: SNMPv2c with a long community string
SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption
SNMPv1 with a non-default community string
SNMP over Telnet
questions.explanation: SNMPv3 supports authentication and privacy through encryption. Versions 1 and 2c send community strings in cleartext regardless of length or default, and Telnet is not a transport for SNMP.

questions.question: A user opens an email attachment and, within minutes, the same malware appears on several other computers on the network without anyone else opening anything. Which malware type is this?
options: Virus
Trojan
Worm
Logic bomb
questions.explanation: A worm propagates on its own across a network. A virus requires a host file and user action to spread, a trojan masquerades as legitimate software and does not self-propagate, and a logic bomb triggers on a condition.

questions.question: Antivirus reports nothing, but an EDR alert shows that PowerShell launched from a Word document is downloading and running code in memory. Which classification BEST fits?
options: A boot sector virus that infects the startup area of the disk
A hardware implant installed in the laptop during manufacture
Fileless malware using living-off-the-land techniques
A macro-free harmless administrative script
questions.explanation: Running in memory and abusing built-in tools describes fileless, living-off-the-land activity, which signature scanners often miss. A boot sector virus infects the startup area, an administrative script launched from a document is not harmless, and nothing suggests hardware tampering.

questions.question: An organization wants the strongest protection against unknown executables on servers that rarely change. Which control is MOST appropriate?
options: Increasing the screen lock timeout
A signature-based blocklist
Disabling the host firewall
Application allowlisting
questions.explanation: Only approved applications run under allowlisting, which suits stable servers. Blocklists stop only known bad software, and the other options either do nothing for execution control or reduce security.

questions.question: A company discovers hundreds of laptops with different, often outdated configurations. Which action BEST establishes a consistent secure posture?
options: Rely on antivirus software alone to keep laptops secure
Let each user configure their own laptop to suit their work, and record the settings in a shared spreadsheet
Disable all logging on the laptops to improve performance
Define a hardened baseline, deploy it with configuration management and monitor for drift
questions.explanation: A baseline enforced and checked by tooling creates consistency and detects deviation. User-managed configurations are inconsistent, antivirus alone does not harden, and disabling logging reduces visibility.

questions.question: A lost laptop contained unencrypted customer data. Which control would have BEST reduced the impact?
options: A longer account lockout threshold on laptop logins
A larger hard drive with more free space
Full-disk encryption with the key protected by a TPM and authentication
A screen saver with a password that locks the laptop after five minutes of inactivity
questions.explanation: Full-disk encryption protects data at rest on a lost device. Lockout settings and screen savers do not protect the drive when it is removed or booted elsewhere, and drive capacity is irrelevant.

questions.question: An employee uses a personal phone to access corporate email. The company wants to be able to remove only corporate data if the employee leaves. Which solution BEST meets this need?
options: MDM or UEM with a managed container and selective wipe
A full factory reset of the personal phone
Requiring employees to forward all email to a personal account
Blocking the phone from the network and issuing nothing
questions.explanation: A managed work container with selective wipe separates corporate and personal data. A full factory reset destroys personal data and is rarely acceptable on a personal device. Forwarding to personal accounts loses control, and blocking provides no access solution.

questions.question: A company moves a customer database from its own servers to an infrastructure-as-a-service virtual machine. Who is responsible for patching the guest operating system?
options: Both share this equally in every case
The customer
The cloud provider
The hypervisor vendor
questions.explanation: In IaaS the provider secures the physical infrastructure and virtualization layer while the customer manages the guest operating system, applications and data. The provider patches the OS in PaaS and SaaS, the responsibility is not equally shared here, and the hypervisor vendor is not involved in the tenant's guest.

questions.question: A security review finds that a cloud storage bucket holding customer records is publicly readable because of a permissive policy. According to the shared responsibility model, who is MOST likely accountable for the exposure?
options: The internet service provider that carries the traffic
The customer, for misconfiguring access to its own data
The end users whose records are stored in the bucket
The cloud provider, for hosting the bucket
questions.explanation: Customers control configuration of their own resources and data, and misconfiguration is the leading cause of cloud exposure. The provider secures the underlying service but does not own the customer's policy decisions, and neither end users nor ISPs configured the bucket.

questions.question: An organization discovers staff using unapproved SaaS file-sharing services to send sensitive documents. Which technology BEST provides visibility and policy enforcement over this activity?
options: A cloud access security broker
A hardware security module
A network time server
A Type 1 hypervisor
questions.explanation: A CASB discovers shadow IT and applies data and access policies to cloud service use. A hypervisor, HSM and time server serve unrelated purposes.

questions.question: Several development virtual machines created for a past project have never been patched and nobody remembers who owns them. Which problem does this describe?
options: Container breakout
VM escape
Hypervisor type confusion
VM sprawl
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled growth of unmanaged virtual machines is VM sprawl and is addressed with inventory, ownership and lifecycle management. VM escape is an attack that breaks guest isolation, and the other terms do not describe unmanaged machines.

questions.question: A team runs many containers on one host. Which practice BEST reduces risk from a vulnerable application inside a container?
options: Run every container as root so that debugging, package installs and file access are easier
Run containers as non-root from minimal, scanned images with restricted capabilities
Disable host logging to save disk space on busy nodes
Store database passwords in the container image so deployments are simple
questions.explanation: Least privilege, small scanned images and restricted capabilities limit what a compromised container can do. Running as root, embedding secrets in images and disabling logging each increase risk.

questions.question: A web application builds SQL queries by concatenating user input into the statement. Which control MOST directly prevents SQL injection?
options: Parameterized queries with input validation
A longer session timeout for logged-in users
Output encoding of HTML in the page templates
Encrypting the database backups before they leave the data centre
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries keep data separate from code so input cannot change the query structure. HTML output encoding addresses cross-site scripting, session timeout concerns session management, and backup encryption protects stored copies rather than live queries.

questions.question: An attacker posts a comment containing a script on a forum, and the script runs in the browsers of other users who view the page. Which attack and primary defence is this?
options: Cross-site request forgery, defended by longer passwords
Buffer overflow, defended by tightening host firewall rules
Cross-site scripting, defended by output encoding and content security policy
SQL injection, defended by parameterized queries and stored procedures in the database layer
questions.explanation: Script that runs in other users' browsers is cross-site scripting, prevented by encoding output and restricting script sources. SQL injection targets the database, cross-site request forgery abuses an authenticated session and is mitigated with anti-forgery tokens, and buffer overflow is a memory corruption problem.

questions.question: A company receives complaints that fraudulent emails appear to come from its domain. Which combination of controls MOST directly lets receivers verify and reject spoofed mail?
options: SPF, DKIM and a DMARC policy
Full-disk encryption on mail servers
A stronger firewall password
An internal certificate authority
questions.explanation: SPF and DKIM authenticate the sending infrastructure and message, and DMARC tells receivers what to do on failure. Firewall passwords, disk encryption and an internal CA do not authenticate mail for external receivers.

questions.question: Which TWO controls are examples of detective controls? (Choose two.)
options: A mantrap at the data centre entrance
Full-disk encryption on laptops
Mandatory vacation for finance staff
Reviewing log files for unusual administrator activity
A written acceptable use policy
questions.explanation: Log review and mandatory vacation both help discover wrongdoing after it occurs: the first by examining records, the second by letting someone else notice irregularities when the usual person is away. A mantrap and disk encryption are preventive, and an acceptable use policy is an administrative directive that mainly deters and guides.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about data classification and handling are correct? (Choose two.)
options: Handling and disposal rules follow from the classification
All data should be labelled at the highest level to be safe
Classification is unnecessary if the data is encrypted
The system administrator sets the classification because they manage the server
The data owner determines the classification level
questions.explanation: The owner classifies, and handling, storage and disposal rules are tied to that label. Administrators are custodians and do not decide sensitivity. Encryption is a protection measure that still depends on knowing what needs protecting, and labelling everything as highest wastes resources and dilutes the scheme.

questions.question: Which TWO situations are MOST likely to be addressed by separation of duties? (Choose two.)
options: A visitor tailgating through a door
An administrator forgetting a password
A server losing power
A developer deploying their own code directly to production without review
One employee both creating vendors and approving payments to them
questions.explanation: Separation of duties prevents one person from controlling every step of a sensitive process, as in vendor creation with payment approval, or writing and releasing code. Forgotten passwords and power loss are availability matters, and tailgating is a physical access problem addressed by mantraps or guards.

questions.question: Which TWO are examples of multi-factor authentication? (Choose two.)
options: A smart card and a PIN
A PIN and a passphrase
A password and a security question
A password and a fingerprint
Two different passwords
questions.explanation: A password with a fingerprint combines knowledge and inherence, and a smart card with a PIN combines possession and knowledge. A password and security question, PIN and passphrase, and two passwords are all knowledge factors, which is one category used repeatedly.

questions.question: An organization is improving its identity lifecycle controls. Which TWO actions would BEST reduce the risk of privilege creep? (Choose two.)
options: Giving new employees the same rights as their predecessor plus extras
Removing prior roles when someone changes jobs
Allowing users to request any access without approval
Periodic access recertification by managers and data owners
Setting passwords to never expire
questions.explanation: Regular reviews and cleaning up old rights at role change directly counter accumulation of unneeded access. Copying a predecessor's rights adds to the problem, non-expiring passwords are a separate matter, and unapproved access requests make creep worse.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about federated identity and OAuth 2.0 are correct? (Choose two.)
options: SAML assertions can let one organization's identity provider vouch for users to another's service
OAuth 2.0 transmits the user's password to the third-party app
OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework for delegated access
OpenID Connect is a replacement for Kerberos tickets
Federation requires every organization to share the same directory
questions.explanation: OAuth 2.0 delegates limited access without sharing passwords, and SAML assertions enable cross-organization trust. OAuth is specifically designed to avoid passing the password to the app, OpenID Connect adds identity on top of OAuth rather than replacing Kerberos, and federation works precisely because organizations keep separate directories.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about vulnerability scanning and penetration testing are correct? (Choose two.)
options: Penetration testing can begin before authorization to save time
A vulnerability scan proves a weakness is exploitable
Scanner severity scores alone determine business risk
A penetration test attempts to exploit weaknesses to demonstrate impact
A credentialed scan generally gives more accurate patch information than a non-credentialed scan
questions.explanation: Penetration tests go beyond finding issues to exploiting them, and credentialed scans see the system from inside. A scan only reports potential weaknesses, written authorization must precede any test, and business risk also depends on exposure and asset value.

questions.question: Which TWO items should be included in a risk register entry? (Choose two.)
options: A guarantee that the risk will not occur
Employees' home addresses
A named risk owner
The attacker's real identity
The chosen treatment decision and its status
questions.explanation: A register tracks an accountable owner and the treatment decision with its progress. Personal home addresses, the attacker's identity and guarantees are not part of risk tracking, and risk can never be guaranteed away.

questions.question: A SIEM implementation is underperforming. Which TWO actions would MOST improve its usefulness? (Choose two.)
options: Stop synchronizing time across sources
Onboard additional relevant log sources and normalize their fields
Disable alerts so analysts are not disturbed
Tune correlation rules to reduce noise and add use cases
Delete logs older than one day to save space
questions.explanation: A SIEM's value comes from the breadth of its log sources and the quality of its correlation. Deleting logs quickly loses evidence, disabling alerts defeats detection, and unsynchronized time makes correlation unreliable.

questions.question: An analyst is collecting evidence from a compromised server. Which TWO actions follow good forensic practice? (Choose two.)
options: Reboot the server to clear suspicious processes first
Collect volatile data such as memory before powering off
Delete the malware to prevent further spread before imaging
Analyze the original disk directly to save time
Document each transfer of evidence for the chain of custody
questions.explanation: Volatile data is captured first and custody is documented at every step. Rebooting and deleting destroy evidence, and analysis should be done on a verified copy rather than the original.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about backup and recovery strategies are correct? (Choose two.)
options: An incremental restore needs only the most recent incremental
A differential restore needs the last full backup plus the most recent differential
A backup that has never been tested is a reliable control
Immutable or offline copies protect backups from ransomware
Backups should reside on the same server they protect for speed
questions.explanation: Differentials accumulate changes since the last full, and immutability or isolation protects copies from tampering. Incremental restores need the full plus every incremental, untested backups cannot be relied on, and keeping backups on the same server defeats their purpose.

questions.question: A company is writing its disaster recovery plan. Which TWO are valid ways to decide an appropriate recovery site? (Choose two.)
options: Choose the cheapest option regardless of requirements
Choose a cold site for any system with a short RTO
Compare the recovery point objective with replication frequency
Choose the site closest to the primary site for convenience
Compare the recovery time objective with the site's activation time
questions.explanation: Site choice must match RTO and RPO. Choosing without regard to requirements risks failing the business, locating the site next to the primary exposes both to the same regional disaster, and cold sites take too long for short recovery times.

questions.question: Which TWO mechanisms allow a receiver to detect that a message was altered in transit? (Choose two.)
options: Compressing the message into a password-protected archive
AES encryption in CBC mode with no authentication tag
An HMAC computed with a secret key shared by sender and receiver
A digital signature created with the sender's private key
Publishing the sender's public key on a website
questions.explanation: A signature and an HMAC both bind the message to a key, so any change fails verification. Unauthenticated CBC encryption provides confidentiality only, and an attacker can modify ciphertext in ways that may go unnoticed. A published public key and a password-protected archive do not by themselves provide verifiable integrity of the message.

questions.question: Which TWO practices are part of sound cryptographic key management? (Choose two.)
options: Never rotating keys to avoid downtime
Rotating keys on a schedule and on suspected compromise
Storing keys in an HSM or key vault separate from the data
Sharing one key among all applications for simplicity
Embedding the key in the application source code
questions.explanation: Protected storage separate from data and planned rotation are the basics. Hard-coded keys leak with the source, shared keys widen the blast radius of compromise, and never rotating keys prolongs exposure.

questions.question: Which TWO controls help prevent VLAN hopping? (Choose two.)
options: Change the native VLAN and avoid using VLAN 1 for user traffic
Allow all switch ports to negotiate trunking automatically
Use the same VLAN for management and users
Turn off logging on the switch
Set unused ports to access mode and disable them
questions.explanation: Disabling unused ports and avoiding default native VLAN use remove the opportunities for switch spoofing and double tagging. Automatic trunk negotiation enables the attack, mixing management with user traffic widens exposure, and turning off logging only reduces visibility.

questions.question: An administrator is hardening network devices. Which TWO settings should be applied? (Choose two.)
options: Send logs to a central server and restrict management to a dedicated network
Replace default credentials and use SSH instead of Telnet
Keep all unused services running for flexibility
Leave SNMPv1 enabled with the community string public
Allow management from any internet address
questions.explanation: Secure credentials and protocols with centralized logging and restricted management access are core hardening steps. SNMPv1 with a default string, open management access and unneeded services expand the attack surface.

questions.question: Which TWO mitigations help defend against a distributed denial-of-service attack? (Choose two.)
options: Upstream scrubbing or a content delivery network with DDoS protection
Increasing password complexity
Encrypting the server's hard disk
Disabling the firewall so traffic flows faster
Rate limiting and SYN cookies at the edge
questions.explanation: Absorbing or filtering volume upstream and limiting abusive connection patterns directly address floods. Password complexity, disabling the firewall and disk encryption do nothing to reduce attack traffic.

questions.question: Which TWO statements correctly describe IPsec? (Choose two.)
options: Authentication Header provides encryption of the payload
Transport mode is used to hide the original IP header
Encapsulating Security Payload provides confidentiality as well as integrity
Tunnel mode is typically used between gateways in site-to-site VPNs
IKE is used to encrypt user data directly
questions.explanation: ESP adds encryption, and tunnel mode encapsulates entire packets between gateways. AH provides integrity and authentication only, transport mode keeps the original header, and IKE negotiates keys and associations rather than carrying user data.

questions.question: Which TWO controls MOST directly help defend endpoints against fileless malware? (Choose two.)
options: Relying only on weekly signature updates
Endpoint detection and response with behaviour monitoring
Disabling the host firewall
Longer password expiration intervals
Script logging and constrained use of PowerShell
questions.explanation: Fileless attacks abuse legitimate tools, so behaviour monitoring and script control are effective. Signature-only approaches miss them, and the firewall and password settings do not address in-memory execution.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about the cloud shared responsibility model are correct? (Choose two.)
options: The customer is always responsible for its own data and access configuration
Moving to the cloud transfers all legal accountability to the provider
In IaaS the provider patches the customer's guest operating system
In SaaS the provider manages more of the stack than in IaaS
The provider is responsible for the customer's identity policies
questions.explanation: Customers keep responsibility for data, identities and configuration, and the provider's share grows from IaaS to PaaS to SaaS. In IaaS the customer patches the guest OS, legal accountability for data remains with the customer, and identity policy is a customer configuration.

questions.question: Which TWO measures reduce the risk of a hypervisor compromise affecting every guest? (Choose two.)
options: Isolate hypervisor management interfaces on a dedicated management network
Disable logging on the host
Patch the hypervisor promptly
Expose the management interface to the internet for convenience
Run all guests with the same root password
questions.explanation: Timely patching and isolated management reduce exposure of the component that all guests depend on. Internet exposure, shared passwords and disabling logs each increase the risk.

questions.question: A web application team is improving secure development practices. Which TWO activities BEST support a secure software development lifecycle? (Choose two.)
options: Threat modelling during design
Letting developers push straight to production without review
Automated static and dynamic security testing in the build pipeline
Adding security controls only after release
Using the same credentials for all environments
questions.explanation: Security belongs at the start through threat modelling and continues through automated testing. Retrofitting after release is costly, bypassing review removes a safeguard, and sharing credentials across environments enlarges the blast radius of any leak.

questions.question: Due care means performing research and investigation before making a decision, such as vetting a supplier.
questions.explanation: That describes due diligence. Due care is acting responsibly and consistently on what was learned, doing what a prudent person would do.

questions.question: A visible security camera can be both a deterrent and a detective control.
questions.explanation: Visibility discourages misconduct, while recordings help identify what happened afterwards. It does not physically prevent entry.

questions.question: Under the ISC2 Code of Ethics, loyalty to an employer outranks protecting the public and the infrastructure.
questions.explanation: The canons are in priority order and protecting society and the common good comes first, so employer loyalty cannot justify harming the public.

questions.question: An electronic lock on an emergency exit should fail secure so that the door stays locked during a power failure.
questions.explanation: Exit doors protecting human life should fail safe, unlocking when power is lost. Fail secure is chosen when asset protection can be balanced with safe egress by other means.

questions.question: Deleting a file and emptying the recycle bin is an acceptable way to sanitize media that held restricted data.
questions.explanation: Deletion only removes pointers, and the data remains recoverable. Sanitization requires clearing, purging or destroying the media according to its sensitivity, as described in NIST SP 800-88.

questions.question: A guideline is a mandatory statement that employees must follow.
questions.explanation: Guidelines are recommended practices. Policies, standards and procedures are the mandatory documents.

questions.question: Defense in depth is strongest when the layered controls are diverse and do not share a single point of failure.
questions.explanation: Independent layers of different types mean one flaw or bypass does not defeat several controls at once.

questions.question: OAuth 2.0 is primarily an authentication protocol that proves who the user is.
questions.explanation: OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework for delegated access. OpenID Connect adds an identity layer for authentication.

questions.question: TACACS+ encrypts the entire packet body, while RADIUS encrypts only the password.
questions.explanation: This is a standard distinction. TACACS+ also separates authentication, authorization and accounting.

questions.question: In discretionary access control, the resource owner decides who may access the resource.
questions.explanation: DAC leaves permission decisions to owners, typically using access control lists, unlike mandatory access control where a central authority sets policy.

questions.question: A security question and a password together constitute multi-factor authentication.
questions.explanation: Both are knowledge factors, so this is still single-factor authentication applied twice.

questions.question: When an employee is dismissed for misconduct, the best first step is to disable access immediately and preserve the account for investigation.
questions.explanation: Immediate disabling removes risk, and preserving the account and its data protects evidence, unlike deleting it.

questions.question: A CVSS score tells you the exact business risk of a vulnerability in your environment.
questions.explanation: CVSS measures technical severity. Business risk also depends on asset value, exposure, existing controls and whether exploitation is occurring.

questions.question: An authenticated (credentialed) vulnerability scan usually produces fewer false positives than an unauthenticated scan.
questions.explanation: Logging in lets the scanner read patch levels and configuration directly instead of inferring them from the outside.

questions.question: Buying cyber insurance eliminates the organization's responsibility for the risk it covers.
questions.explanation: Insurance transfers part of the financial impact, but the organization remains responsible for protecting the asset and for reputational and legal consequences.

questions.question: A false negative in a detection system is usually the more dangerous error because a real threat goes unnoticed.
questions.explanation: False positives cost analyst time, but missed detections create false confidence and allow attackers to continue.

questions.question: If the annualized loss expectancy of a risk is 20,000 dollars, spending 30,000 dollars a year on a control that removes the risk entirely is cost-justified.
questions.explanation: The most the control can save is 20,000 a year, which is less than its cost. A control is justified when the reduction in ALE exceeds its cost.

questions.question: The recovery point objective defines the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time.
questions.explanation: RPO drives backup and replication frequency, while RTO addresses how long restoration may take.

questions.question: A compromised server should be powered off immediately so that the attacker cannot do more damage, even if memory contents are lost.
questions.explanation: Powering off destroys volatile evidence. Network isolation contains the system while preserving memory and connection state for analysis.

questions.question: A parallel disaster recovery test runs recovery systems alongside production without interrupting it.
questions.explanation: It validates the recovery environment with low risk, unlike a full interruption test that halts production.

questions.question: An incremental backup strategy lets you restore using only the full backup and the latest incremental.
questions.explanation: Incrementals hold only changes since the previous backup, so a restore needs the full backup and every incremental since.

questions.question: The recovery time objective must be shorter than the maximum tolerable downtime.
questions.explanation: If restoration takes longer than the business can tolerate, harm occurs before recovery, so the RTO sits inside the MTD.

questions.question: A post-incident review should focus mainly on identifying and punishing the person responsible for the error.
questions.explanation: Reviews should be blameless and improvement-focused, producing changes to controls, detection and procedures.

questions.question: A hash function can be reversed to recover the original input if you have the right key.
questions.explanation: Hashes are one-way and keyless. Encryption is reversible with a key; hashing provides integrity checking rather than confidentiality.

questions.question: To create a digital signature, a sender uses their own private key.
questions.explanation: The receiver verifies it with the sender's public key, which proves origin and integrity and gives non-repudiation.

questions.question: Forward secrecy means that compromise of a server's long-term private key does not expose previously recorded session traffic.
questions.explanation: Ephemeral key exchange gives each session an independent key, which TLS 1.3 requires.

questions.question: ECB is the recommended block cipher mode for encrypting large structured data because it is simple and fast.
questions.explanation: ECB leaks patterns because identical blocks encrypt identically. Authenticated modes such as GCM are recommended.

questions.question: Network address translation provides the same protection as a stateful firewall.
questions.explanation: NAT hides internal addresses and enables sharing public addresses, but it does not by itself enforce a security policy.

questions.question: DNSSEC provides integrity and authenticity of DNS responses but does not encrypt the queries.
questions.explanation: It signs records so tampering can be detected. Privacy of the query requires DNS over TLS or HTTPS.

questions.question: A span port on a switch lets an intrusion prevention system actively block malicious traffic.
questions.explanation: A span port gives a passive copy of traffic. Blocking requires an inline placement.

questions.question: WPA3 improves protection against offline password guessing compared with WPA2 Personal.
questions.explanation: WPA3 uses Simultaneous Authentication of Equals, so captured handshakes cannot be attacked offline in the same way.

questions.question: Split tunnelling sends all of a remote user's traffic through the corporate VPN.
questions.explanation: That is full tunnelling. Split tunnelling sends only corporate-bound traffic through the VPN and the rest directly to the internet.

questions.question: IEEE 802.1X can prevent an unauthorized device from gaining network access by simply plugging into a switch port.
questions.explanation: The port stays unauthorized until the supplicant authenticates through the authenticator to the authentication server.

questions.question: In an infrastructure-as-a-service deployment the customer is responsible for patching the guest operating system.
questions.explanation: The provider secures the infrastructure and virtualization layer, while the customer manages everything above it.

questions.question: Containers share the host operating system kernel, so a kernel vulnerability can affect all containers on that host.
questions.explanation: Containers are lighter than virtual machines because they share the kernel, which also reduces isolation.

questions.question: Application allowlisting only blocks software that is already known to be malicious.
questions.explanation: That describes blocklisting. Allowlisting permits only approved applications and blocks everything else by default.

questions.question: Cross-site scripting is best prevented with parameterized database queries.
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries prevent SQL injection. Cross-site scripting is mitigated by output encoding, input validation and content security policy.

questions.question: A cloud access security broker can help an organization discover and control the use of unapproved cloud applications.
questions.explanation: CASBs provide visibility into shadow IT and enforce data protection and access policy on cloud services.

questions.question: A company's internal code of conduct tells staff to keep a known product flaw secret from customers until a major sales event. An SSCP-certified analyst learns of it. What is the MOST appropriate course of action?
options: Do nothing for now, because a flaw that has not been exploited creates no ethical obligation
Quietly tell a competitor about the flaw so that customers hear of it from someone else
Follow the company code, because organizational rules outrank professional canons while employed there
Decline to take part in concealing it and escalate through the proper internal channel
questions.explanation: The ISC2 canons put the public and infrastructure first, so an employer rule cannot justify concealing a risk to customers, and the analyst raises it through the right channel. Treating the company code as superior ignores the canon order. Leaking to a competitor is neither honorable nor a proper channel, and the lack of exploitation does not remove the duty.

questions.question: A legacy production controller cannot accept security patches and the vendor will not fix a known weakness. Management wants to keep running it. Which approach BEST reflects a compensating control?
options: Isolate it behind a restrictive firewall, add monitoring and document the exception with an expiry date
Install the latest antivirus product on an engineering workstation that sits next to the controller and scan its files remotely each night
Accept the risk informally in an email thread with the operations team and take no other action
Remove the controller from the asset inventory so that vulnerability scanners stop reporting on it
questions.explanation: A compensating control gives comparable protection through other means and is documented, approved and time-limited. An antivirus tool on a neighbouring machine does not protect the controller. Removing it from the inventory hides the problem, and an informal email is not a formal risk acceptance with an accountable owner.

questions.question: A company signs a customer contract that requires it to follow a specific payment card security standard. What should the security practitioner do FIRST?
options: Wait for the customer's auditor to arrive and list everything that is missing from the environment
Buy a monitoring product whose marketing says it makes a company compliant with the standard
Encrypt every file server in the company regardless of whether it ever holds payment card data
Scope the systems that handle card data and map the requirements to existing controls to find gaps
questions.explanation: Compliance work starts by scoping what handles the regulated data and mapping requirements to controls, which shows the gaps and the owners. A product on its own cannot establish compliance. Waiting for an auditor is reactive, and encrypting everything without scoping wastes effort and may miss the actual requirements.

questions.question: The vendor of the operating system on several file servers announces that support ends in six months. What is the BEST response?
options: Plan a migration now and isolate any survivors under a time-limited, documented risk acceptance
Disable logging on the servers so that the number of alerts about the old system falls
Continue as normal and revisit the question after the date, because the servers have run for years without any security incident
Replace the servers on the day support ends using a fresh image that has not been tested
questions.explanation: End-of-support systems stop receiving patches, so replacement is planned ahead and any remaining systems get compensating controls and a formal, time-limited exception. Continuing unchanged ignores the growing exposure, disabling logging removes detection, and an untested last-day swap risks outages.

questions.question: A development team adds an open-source library to a commercial product to save time. Which activity BEST manages the risk this creates?
options: Ask the library's authors to review and approve the full source code of the commercial product
Review the licence terms and track the component with software composition analysis
Assume that any widely used library is free of both vulnerabilities and licence conditions
Copy the code into the product and delete the licence file so that customers do not ask questions
questions.explanation: Third-party components need licence review and ongoing vulnerability tracking, which is what software composition analysis supports. Popularity does not guarantee security or compatible terms, stripping the licence breaks its conditions, and the authors have no role in approving your product.

questions.question: A request to change the schema of the production payroll database has been approved by the business owner. What should still happen BEFORE the change is implemented?
options: Permanent removal of all the older schema backups to save storage
A new data classification label for every table in the payroll team database
A lessons-learned meeting about how the change went afterwards
A security impact analysis, with testing and a rollback plan
questions.explanation: Impact analysis, testing and rollback planning are completed before implementation so risk to the system and its controls is understood. A lessons-learned meeting happens afterwards. Reclassifying data does not address the technical risk, and deleting previous backups would remove the rollback path.

questions.question: A company returns leased multifunction printers at the end of the lease. The devices have internal drives that stored scanned HR documents. Which action BEST addresses the data risk?
options: Return the printers as they are and trust the leasing company to clear them later on
Reset the printer's network settings to factory defaults and leave its internal drive untouched
Sanitize or destroy the drives and get documented proof before the devices leave the site
Delete the scan folders from the central print server that the printers used to send files to
questions.explanation: Storage inside returned equipment must be sanitized or destroyed under the organization's control, with evidence such as a certificate. Trusting the lessor transfers the risk without assurance. Deleting folders on a server does not touch the printer's internal drive, and a network settings reset leaves stored images intact.

questions.question: A visitor with a temporary badge is found alone in a corridor that leads to the server room. What is the BEST immediate action?
options: Politely challenge the visitor, escort them back to their host and report the lapse
Confiscate the visitor's phone and search their bag before allowing them to leave the corridor
Ignore it, because anyone wearing a temporary badge has already been approved to walk around
Disable every badge reader in the building until the visitor management system has been audited
questions.explanation: Visitors must be escorted in sensitive areas, so the right response is a courteous challenge, an escort and a report so that the process gap is fixed. Treating the badge as sufficient ignores the escort rule, a search goes beyond staff authority, and disabling readers causes a bigger problem.

questions.question: A team wants security testing to catch flaws earlier in software delivery. Which DevSecOps practice MOST directly supports this?
options: Skipping peer code review for small changes so that the pipeline moves faster
A single penetration test performed once, after the software has been released to customers
Automated static, dependency and secrets scans on each build
Giving developers production administrator rights so that they can fix issues more quickly
questions.explanation: Automating scans in the pipeline finds flaws when they are cheapest to fix. A single post-release test finds problems late. Developer administrator rights on production break separation of duties, and skipping review removes a safeguard.

questions.question: Customer support records have passed the end of their documented retention period. No litigation is pending and no legal hold exists. What should the organization do?
options: Keep them indefinitely in case they become useful to some team at a later date
Move them to a personal cloud account that one of the managers uses for safekeeping
Move them to the busiest shared file server so that they keep being backed up each night
Securely destroy them under the retention schedule and record the destruction
questions.explanation: With the retention period over and no hold, records are destroyed securely and the destruction is documented, which limits exposure. Keeping data forever increases breach and discovery risk, and moving it to personal or shared locations loses control.

questions.question: Which TWO are administrative controls? (Choose two.)
options: A written data handling standard
An access control vestibule at the lab door
A next-generation firewall policy
Full-disk encryption on laptops
A background screening requirement for new hires
questions.explanation: Screening requirements and written standards are policies and procedures, which are administrative (managerial) controls. A firewall policy and disk encryption are technical controls, and the vestibule is a physical control.

questions.question: Which TWO practices support good visitor and facility management for a data center? (Choose two.)
options: Propping the loading door open during deliveries
Sharing badge PINs among the operations team
Letting visitors keep a reusable badge for convenience
Escorting visitors and recording their entry and exit
Restricting cameras and personal storage devices in the equipment room
