questions.explanation: Escorts with logs and limits on cameras and storage devices reduce theft, photography and malware introduction. Reusable visitor badges, open doors and shared PINs all erode physical control and accountability.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about change and configuration management are correct? (Choose two.)
options: Configuration baselines are only needed for network devices
Configuration management compares running systems with an approved baseline to find drift
The implementer should be the only approver of their own change
A security impact analysis is completed before a change is approved
Emergency changes never need documentation
questions.explanation: Baselines make drift visible, and impact analysis belongs before approval. Self-approval removes separation of duties, emergency changes are documented, usually after the fact, and baselines apply to servers, endpoints, cloud resources and devices alike.

questions.question: A tabletop exercise requires taking production systems offline to be valid.
questions.explanation: A tabletop is a discussion-based walk-through of a scenario. It tests plans, roles and decisions without affecting production.

questions.question: Open-source software does not need licence review because anyone may use it freely.
questions.explanation: Open-source licences carry conditions, and some copyleft licences impose obligations on redistribution. Components should still be reviewed and tracked for vulnerabilities.

questions.question: A security impact analysis for a change is performed after the change goes live to confirm what happened.
questions.explanation: The analysis informs the approval decision, so it is done before implementation. A review after the change is a post-implementation review.

questions.question: A system that no longer receives vendor patches can stay in service unchanged as long as an antivirus product is installed.
questions.explanation: Antivirus cannot replace missing patches. End-of-support systems need replacement or isolation with compensating controls and a documented, time-limited risk acceptance.

questions.question: Retention schedules mean data should be kept as long as required by law, contract and business need, and no longer, unless a legal hold applies.
questions.explanation: Over-retention raises breach and discovery exposure, while under-retention breaks legal duties. A legal hold suspends normal destruction.

questions.question: A team proposes allowing only devices with approved MAC addresses onto the corporate wired network and calling this device authentication. What is the BEST criticism?
options: A MAC address is easily copied, so it identifies a device without proving its identity
A MAC address is long enough to be guessed by brute force within a few minutes
A MAC address filter cannot be applied to wired ports and works only on wireless access points
A MAC address changes every time a device reboots, which makes the list impossible to maintain
questions.explanation: Addresses are visible on the wire and can be set by software, so an attacker simply copies an approved one. Certificate-based authentication with 802.1X proves possession of a private key instead. MAC filtering works on wired and wireless networks, addresses do not change at each reboot, and guessing is not the usual attack.

questions.question: A partner company needs to sign in to your internal expense portal using its own corporate credentials without you creating accounts for its staff. In a SAML federation, which component issues the assertion that your portal relies on?
options: The partner's identity provider
Your internal portal acting as a service provider and issuing assertions about its own users
The partner's end user device acting as a certificate authority for its staff
A DNS server that signs responses for the partner's domain name
questions.explanation: The identity provider authenticates its own users and issues a signed assertion, and your portal, as the service provider, validates it. The service provider consumes assertions rather than issuing them. A DNS server and a user device are not part of the federation trust.

questions.question: A mobile application must learn who the signed-in user is, not just obtain permission to read a calendar. Which mechanism is designed for this and builds on OAuth 2.0?
options: OpenID Connect and its ID token
A longer-lived OAuth 2.0 refresh token with every available scope
A Kerberos service ticket issued by the key distribution centre
A RADIUS accounting message sent to the network access server
questions.explanation: OpenID Connect adds an authentication layer to OAuth 2.0 and returns an ID token describing the user. An OAuth access or refresh token only conveys delegated permissions and is not meant to identify the user. RADIUS accounting records sessions, and a Kerberos ticket is used inside a Kerberos realm.

questions.question: A supplier needs to upload invoices to a web portal and check their status. Where should the portal be placed to limit risk to the internal network?
options: In a DMZ or extranet segment, with restrictive firewall rules to internal systems
On the internal server network, with the supplier connecting through a split-tunnel VPN
On every employee workstation, so each can receive invoices directly from suppliers
On the guest wireless network that visitors use, to keep the portal away from internal staff
questions.explanation: A DMZ or extranet segment exposes only the portal and lets firewalls control what it can reach inside. Placing it on the internal network gives a compromised portal broad reach. The guest network mixes untrusted users with a business service, and putting it on workstations multiplies the attack surface.

questions.question: A cloud calendar add-on asks for permission to read and write every mailbox in the organization, although it only needs to show free and busy times. What is the BEST response?
options: Approve it for a week and see whether anything unusual appears in the logs
Approve it and tell every employee to use a longer password for their mailbox
Approve it, because the vendor is well known and the add-on is popular
Decline the broad request and approve only the narrow calendar scope it needs
questions.explanation: Least privilege applies to delegated access: grant only the minimum scope for the function. Reputation does not justify excess rights, a trial week gives an attacker time to use them, and a longer password does nothing about a token that already holds the access.

questions.question: Domain A trusts domain B through a one-way trust, with A as the trusting domain. Which statement is correct?
options: Accounts in both domains can access resources in each other's domain without any further configuration
Accounts in A can be granted access to resources in B, but accounts in B cannot be granted access in A
Accounts in B can be granted access to resources in A, but accounts in A cannot be granted access in B
No account in either domain can be given access to a resource in the other domain
questions.explanation: The trusting domain holds the resources and accepts authentication from the trusted domain, so the trusted domain's users can be granted access. The reverse direction is not covered by a one-way trust. Mutual access describes a two-way trust, and a trust that allows nothing would serve no purpose.

questions.question: A recruiter asks IT to create an account for a remote contractor who has only emailed a photograph of an identity card. Which step is MOST appropriate before issuing credentials?
options: Ask the contractor to choose a long passphrase, because a strong password proves identity
Verify identity with a stronger process, such as checking documents against an authoritative source
Issue the shared contractor account that the whole project team already uses to avoid delays
Create the account now and rely on the first password reset to confirm who the contractor really is
questions.explanation: Identity proofing confirms the real person behind the request before a credential exists, and an emailed photograph is weak evidence. A password reset or passphrase proves nothing about who the applicant is, and a shared account destroys accountability.

questions.question: An audit finds enabled accounts for staff who left months ago, because the directory is updated by hand. Which improvement BEST prevents this?
options: Drive joiner, mover and leaver changes from HR and reconcile accounts regularly
Move every account into a single group so there is only one list to check
Ask managers to send an email to the help desk whenever they remember that someone on their team has left
Force all users to change their passwords every thirty days
questions.explanation: Driving the lifecycle from the authoritative source and reconciling regularly removes manual delay and finds orphaned accounts. Relying on memory is what failed, frequent password changes do not remove accounts of people who left, and a single group destroys least privilege.

questions.question: A reviewer finds that a user has write access to a finance share although nobody ever granted it directly. The access comes through several nested groups. What does this BEST illustrate?
options: A failed biometric enrolment that produced a high false acceptance rate
A routine example of mandatory access control labelling
Inherited entitlements, which need reviewing as effective access
A deliberate use of just-in-time privileged access
questions.explanation: Rights can accumulate through group nesting, so effective access, not just direct grants, must be reviewed. Biometric error rates, mandatory labels and just-in-time access describe other things entirely.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about device authentication are correct? (Choose two.)
options: A MAC address can be spoofed, so it should not be the only proof of device identity
A certificate whose private key is stored in a TPM is hard to copy to another device
Device certificates cannot be revoked once issued
Device authentication removes the need to authenticate users
A MAC address is a cryptographic secret known only to the device
questions.explanation: A TPM-protected key gives a device a hard-to-clone identity, and spoofable MAC addresses are only identifiers. A MAC address is public on the wire, certificates can be revoked, and user authentication is still needed because it answers a different question.

questions.question: Which TWO controls MOST reduce the risk from third-party API and app integrations? (Choose two.)
options: Hard-code integration secrets in scripts so they never expire
Issue each integration its own credentials with the narrowest scopes it needs
Log and review integration activity, and re-approve it when permissions change
Share one administrative API key between all integrations to simplify management
Grant broad read and write scopes now in case they are needed later
questions.explanation: Narrow, individual credentials and ongoing monitoring limit what a compromised integration can do and help detect it. Shared admin keys, speculative broad scopes and hard-coded secrets all increase exposure.

questions.question: Filtering network access by MAC address is a strong form of device authentication.
questions.explanation: MAC addresses can be copied or changed by software. Certificate-based authentication with a protected private key is far stronger.

questions.question: A transitive trust lets trust extend through a chain of domains, so a compromise in one domain can potentially reach another.
questions.explanation: If A trusts B and B trusts C, A trusts C. Because of this, trusts should be limited to what the business needs.

questions.question: Identity proofing is the step that is repeated every time a user logs in.
questions.explanation: Proofing confirms a real-world identity at enrolment before credentials are issued. Authentication is what happens at each login.

questions.question: An extranet gives anonymous members of the public unrestricted access to internal resources.
questions.explanation: An extranet gives controlled, authenticated access to selected partners or customers. Anonymous public access to internal resources would be a serious failure.

questions.question: A bank's analyst wants peer banks to ingest indicators from a phishing campaign automatically into their tools. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
options: Send a printed summary of the indicators to peers by courier each month
Email a spreadsheet of indicators to each peer, one at a time, every week
Publish the indicators in STIX format and exchange them over TAXII
Post the full incident report on the bank's public website for all to read
questions.explanation: STIX is the structured language and TAXII the transport for automated sharing. Manual spreadsheets and printed summaries are slow and prone to error, and a public posting may expose sensitive internal details that a trusted sharing channel and Traffic Light Protocol marking would protect.

questions.question: A SOC lead wants to know which attacker behaviours the current detection rules would miss. Which use of MITRE ATT&CK is BEST?
options: Treat it as a regulation that the organization must be certified against each year
Use the framework's severity numbers to compute the annual loss expectancy
Replace the SIEM with the framework, because it already contains detection content
Map detection rules to ATT&CK techniques and look for techniques with no coverage
questions.explanation: ATT&CK is a catalogue of adversary tactics and techniques, so mapping detections to it exposes coverage gaps. It does not score risk or loss, is not a certifiable regulation, and is a knowledge base that complements rather than replaces tools.

questions.question: During a design review, a threat modeler notes that an attacker on the network could change the amounts in payment messages between two services without being noticed. Which STRIDE category is this?
options: Tampering
Repudiation, because the sender could later deny having sent the messages
Information disclosure, because the attacker can read the payment messages in transit
Spoofing, because the attacker pretends to be the sender of the payment messages
questions.explanation: Altering data in transit violates integrity, which is tampering. Spoofing is about false identity, repudiation is the ability to deny an action, and information disclosure concerns reading data rather than changing it.

questions.question: In the NIST Risk Management Framework, a system owner reviews the types of data a new system will process and assigns it an impact level of moderate. Which step is this?
options: Implement, where the selected controls are put into place on the system
Authorize, where a senior official accepts the risk of operating the system
Monitor, where controls are watched on an ongoing basis after go-live
Categorize
questions.explanation: Categorizing the system by the impact of losing confidentiality, integrity and availability comes before selecting controls. Authorization is the later formal risk decision, monitoring continues after go-live, and implementation puts selected controls in place.

questions.question: Which statement is an example of a risk TOLERANCE rather than a risk appetite?
options: The company is willing to take moderate risk to enter new markets quickly
The board wants security to support business growth wherever it can
Leadership prefers innovation over caution when launching new products
The order system must not be down for more than four hours in any incident
questions.explanation: A tolerance is a measurable limit on variation for a specific objective, here maximum downtime. The other statements are broad appetite statements about the kind and amount of risk leadership is willing to pursue.

questions.question: A manager decides that a known weakness in an old application is not worth discussing because the fix would be costly, and nothing is recorded. How should this be described and handled?
options: Risk avoidance, because the manager chose not to deal with the application at all
Risk transfer, because the cost of the fix was pushed onto the application team
Ignoring the risk; assess it, then treat it or formally accept it with sign-off
Risk acceptance, which is complete because the manager made the decision alone
questions.explanation: Accepting a risk requires a documented decision by someone with authority within appetite. Silent neglect leaves no owner and no record, so the risk is assessed and a proper treatment or formal acceptance is made. Transfer needs a third party such as an insurer, and avoidance means ending the activity.

questions.question: A vulnerability scanner reports a CVSS v4.0 base score of 9.3 for a flaw on an isolated test server holding no data. How should the score be interpreted?
options: It is Critical severity, but isolation and the lack of data lower the risk
It is invalid, because base scores apply only to internet-facing systems
It is Low severity, because the server is isolated and holds no sensitive data
It is exactly the business risk to the company, so the server must be patched first
questions.explanation: A 9.0 to 10.0 base score is Critical severity, but severity is not risk, and the asset's value and exposure reduce its priority. Isolation does not change the severity band, the score is not a statement of business risk, and base scores are defined regardless of exposure.

questions.question: A company discovers that attackers copied personal data of residents of several EU countries. The incident is likely to put those individuals at risk. What should the company do under GDPR?
options: Notify the supervisory authority without undue delay, within 72 hours where feasible
Wait until the forensic investigation is fully complete before telling any regulator
Delete the affected records at once so that no notification is legally required
Notify only the affected individuals, because authorities hear only about financial data
questions.explanation: GDPR sets a notification clock of 72 hours from awareness where feasible, and the controller continues investigating while notifying. Waiting for the end of the investigation misses the deadline, authorities are notified about personal data breaches generally, and deleting records destroys evidence and does not remove the duty.

questions.question: A vendor will process customer data in a data center in another country. Which concern should the security team raise FIRST with legal and procurement?
options: Which country's laws apply, including access by authorities, and whether transfers are lawful
Whether the vendor's marketing website and sales brochures use modern fonts, attractive images and consistent branding
Whether the vendor's logo can be displayed on the company's partner page
Whether the vendor will accept payment by corporate card instead of invoice
questions.explanation: Location determines jurisdiction, government access rights and transfer restrictions, so this is the key legal and privacy concern. Fonts, logos and payment methods do not affect legal exposure over the data.

questions.question: The company is about to give a new software-as-a-service provider access to customer records. Which evidence is MOST useful in its supplier risk review?
options: An independent assurance report on the service, plus breach notice and audit right clauses
The provider's sales presentation, which describes its security as industry leading and lists many awards
A testimonial from another customer that uses the service for a different purpose
The total number of employees the provider has in its security department
questions.explanation: Independent assurance for the actual service and enforceable contract terms give verifiable evidence and recourse. A sales deck, a testimonial and headcount are claims, not evidence of controls that protect your data.

questions.question: A design review of a new application finds a single database server with no replica, and all administrative interfaces exposed on the user network. What does this BEST represent?
options: Architecture weaknesses: a single point of failure and exposed management access
A mature design that already follows the principle of defense in depth
A successful penetration test that exploited the database server
Evidence that no data classification scheme has been applied anywhere in the whole project
questions.explanation: An architecture review looks for single points of failure and exposed management paths, both found here. No exploitation occurred, so it is not a test result, classification is unrelated to what was seen, and the design lacks, rather than shows, layered defense.

questions.question: Which observation is MOST clearly an event of interest that should trigger investigation?
options: A firewall rule was changed at 2 a.m. by an unexpected account with no change ticket
A user signed in successfully at the usual start of the working day from the office network
A workstation received its monthly operating system update on the usual schedule
A scheduled backup job finished within its normal time window overnight
questions.explanation: An unauthorized, undocumented configuration change by an unexpected account is exactly what monitoring should flag. The other items are normal, expected activity that matches the baseline.

questions.question: A company's servers keep their logs only on their own disks. After a compromise the attacker deletes them. Which design change BEST prevents this?
options: Rename the log folder on each server to something that is less obvious
Increase the size of the local log files and of the disk that holds them so that deleting them takes the attacker longer
Forward events in near real time to a central collector that has restricted write access
Enable verbose logging only on the servers that have not yet been compromised
questions.explanation: Off-host, centrally protected copies remain even if the attacker controls the original system. Larger local files, renamed folders and logging on other servers leave the evidence under the attacker's control.

questions.question: Investigators say they often need to look back ten months, and regulations require twelve months for authentication records. What should the retention policy specify for those records?
options: Keep them for ten months, because investigators' needs override regulations
Keep them thirty days, because older logs are never useful to an investigation
Keep them at least twelve months in protected storage, longer under a legal hold
Keep them only until the log storage fills, then overwrite the oldest entries first
questions.explanation: Retention is set by the longest legal, regulatory and investigative need and held securely, with holds extending it. Thirty days or overwrite-when-full ignore the requirement, and investigative preference does not override a regulatory minimum.

questions.question: One failed sign-in to a VPN account is common noise. An analyst wants an alert only when many failed sign-ins are followed by a success from a country the user has never used. Which SIEM capability provides this?
options: Compressing the log files to reduce long-term storage costs
Sending every individual failed sign-in to the on-call engineer's phone
Correlation rules that combine events across time and sources
Raising the log retention period for the VPN appliance to a full year
questions.explanation: Correlation turns separate low-value events into one meaningful alert and reduces noise. Retention, compression and paging on every event do not combine the events, and the last would create overwhelming noise.

questions.question: An analyst confirms ransomware activity on a finance server. The incident procedure lists severity levels and who must be told at each level. What should the analyst do?
options: Wait until the next weekly report to mention the finding to senior management
Escalate as the procedure requires for that severity and record the timing
Ask the finance server's owner to decide whether this counts as an incident
Message only the finance team, because the affected data belongs to them
questions.explanation: Escalation follows documented criteria so the right people act quickly, with a record kept. Waiting for a weekly report delays response, telling only one team skips the incident process, and the owner cannot override severity criteria.

questions.question: Which TWO items belong in a supplier risk review for a provider that will hold customer data? (Choose two.)
options: The provider's slogan and advertising awards
The colour scheme of the provider's dashboard
Contract clauses covering breach notification and audit rights
An independent assurance report whose scope includes the service being bought
The number of social media followers the provider has
questions.explanation: Enforceable terms and independent evidence for the actual service are the substance of a supplier review. Marketing slogans, interface colours and follower counts say nothing about controls.

questions.question: Which TWO are correct uses of threat intelligence indicators of compromise (IOCs)? (Choose two.)
options: Treating an IOC as valid forever, whatever its age
Searching logs and endpoints for known malicious hashes or domains
Using IOCs in place of any behavioural detection
Publishing internal passwords as indicators for sharing
Adding known malicious addresses to blocking rules and alerts
questions.explanation: IOCs are searched for and blocked or alerted on to find or stop known threats. They age quickly, so they cannot be relied on forever or used as the only detection, and internal secrets are never shared as indicators.

questions.question: Which TWO practices make logs more trustworthy as evidence? (Choose two.)
options: Letting each administrator edit their own logs to correct mistakes
Sending copies to a central store that administrators of the source systems cannot alter
Synchronizing clocks across sources with NTP
Using local time zones that differ between sources
Keeping logs only on the system that created them
questions.explanation: Consistent time and tamper-resistant central storage support reliable timelines and integrity. Editable logs, mixed time zones and local-only storage weaken trust in the record.

questions.question: Which TWO are good reasons to tune SIEM rules? (Choose two.)
options: Alerts make analysts feel busy, so more of them is better
Known-benign activity generates repeated alerts that bury real ones
Disabling a noisy rule is the best way to remove false positives
New critical systems or attack techniques need detection coverage
Rules never need review once they are written
questions.explanation: Tuning removes noise from benign activity and adds coverage for new assets and techniques. Volume is not value, a rule should be understood and refined before being disabled, and rules need periodic review.

questions.question: Ignoring a risk is equivalent to formally accepting it, as long as management is aware of it informally.
questions.explanation: Acceptance is a documented decision by an authorized owner within appetite. Informal awareness leaves no record, owner or review.

questions.question: A CVSS base score expresses technical severity and does not by itself tell you the business risk in your environment.
questions.explanation: Business risk also depends on exposure, asset value, existing controls and whether exploitation is active. Threat and Environmental metrics help adjust it.

questions.question: Risk appetite is a precise numerical limit for one specific objective, such as maximum downtime in hours.
questions.explanation: That describes risk tolerance. Appetite is the broader amount and type of risk leadership is willing to pursue to meet objectives.

questions.question: Indicators of compromise such as IP addresses and file hashes tend to go stale quickly, while attacker behaviours last longer.
questions.explanation: Adversaries change infrastructure and files easily, so behaviour-based detection mapped to techniques such as those in MITRE ATT&CK is more durable.

questions.question: Where a breach is likely to put EU individuals at risk, GDPR requires telling the supervisory authority without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours of becoming aware.
questions.explanation: The clock starts at awareness, and the controller can add details later as the investigation proceeds.

questions.question: A logging policy should state what is logged, how long logs are kept and how their integrity is protected.
questions.explanation: Those elements make logs consistent, available when needed and trustworthy as evidence.

questions.question: Silencing a noisy alert is always the right response, because fewer alerts mean a healthier SIEM.
questions.explanation: Understand why the alert fires first. Over-tuning can hide real attacks and create false negatives, which are usually the more dangerous error.

questions.question: An analyst reviews an alert and decides that suspicious activity on a server is a confirmed security incident of medium severity and assigns it to the response team. Which ISO/IEC 27035 phase is this?
options: Prepare, because the team is being assigned to work on the case
Assess and decide
Detect and report, because the alert was the first sign of trouble
Learn lessons, because the analyst has formed a view of what occurred
questions.explanation: Judging whether an event is an incident and how severe it is belongs to assess and decide. Preparation is the work done before incidents, learning lessons is the post-incident review, and detect and report is the earlier stage where the alert is first noticed and passed on.

questions.question: A journalist telephones a security analyst and asks whether the company has suffered a breach. What should the analyst do?
options: Offer a technical explanation of how the attackers probably got in
Decline to comment and refer the journalist to the designated spokesperson
Confirm the details that the analyst knows, so the story is accurate
Deny that anything has happened until the whole investigation is finished
questions.explanation: External messaging goes through the designated spokesperson with legal review, so the analyst refers the call. Confirming details or explaining the attack path discloses unreviewed information, and denying something that may be true is dishonest and risks later damage.

questions.question: A company is sued by a former supplier over a contract dispute, and it wants to use log evidence in court. Which standard of proof normally applies in this civil case?
options: Beyond a reasonable doubt, as in any case with evidence from computers
No standard applies, because digital evidence is accepted automatically
Absolute certainty, supported by at least two independent forensic experts
Preponderance of the evidence, meaning more likely than not
questions.explanation: Civil cases generally use the preponderance of evidence. Beyond reasonable doubt is the criminal standard, no case requires absolute certainty or two experts, and digital evidence must still be shown to be reliable and authentic.

questions.question: A first responder arrives at a desk where a suspect workstation is powered on, showing an open document and a chat window. According to good practice, what should the responder do FIRST?
options: Record the screen and the scene, then follow the plan for isolation and hand-off
Close the open windows and log the user out to protect the open files
Run a full antivirus scan on it to see whether any malware is present
Shut the machine down at once by pulling the power so that nothing else on it can be changed or lost
questions.explanation: Recording the state preserves what is visible and volatile before anything is altered, then the plan for isolation and examiner hand-off is followed. Powering off loses memory, closing windows and logging out change the state, and running a scan alters files and timestamps.

questions.question: An examiner is asked to report to a court on the contents of a seized laptop. Which characteristic is MOST important for the report?
options: A narrative written from memory several weeks after the examination
A confident conclusion that fully supports the side that engaged the examiner, with contrary evidence left out
Objective, reproducible findings with methods stated and fact kept apart from opinion
A short summary that leaves out limits of the analysis to avoid any confusion
questions.explanation: Credibility rests on repeatable methods and an honest division between facts and opinion. Favouring the client breaks impartiality, omitting limitations hides weaknesses, and a report written from memory lacks reliability compared with contemporaneous notes.

questions.question: Human resources asks the security team to read an employee's mailbox because the employee is suspected of leaking documents. What should the security team do BEFORE collecting anything?
options: Confirm that policy and law allow the review and get written sign-off from legal and HR
Ask the employee's manager to log in as the employee and look around
Start with the employee's personal webmail account in case it is easier to search
Copy the whole mailbox first and ask for approval afterwards, so that nothing can be deleted before approval arrives
questions.explanation: Authority comes first, because unauthorized access during an investigation can be unlawful and taint evidence. Collecting first, borrowing the employee's login and reaching into personal accounts all go beyond authorized scope.

questions.question: A long-running outbreak of illness means that most staff cannot attend the office for several months. Which continuity measure MOST directly addresses this?
options: Remote work with tested capacity and cross-training so critical roles have backups
Changing the passwords on all of the shared service accounts immediately
Moving the primary data center to a hot site in the same city as the office, to improve recovery of the facilities
Buying additional insurance and making no changes to the way operations run
questions.explanation: Pandemic planning focuses on keeping people able to work and critical roles covered, which means remote capacity and cross-trained staff. A hot site in the same city addresses facilities, insurance does not keep operations running, and password changes do not help staff availability.

questions.question: After a data center fire, a recovery team has to bring services back in order. Which approach is BEST?
options: Restore in BIA priority order, starting with the network and identity services others rely on
Restore the application with the loudest and most senior users first, whatever it happens to depend on
Restore the oldest systems first, because they have been running in service the longest
Restore everything at the same time so that nothing waits for anything else
questions.explanation: Restoration follows business priority and dependencies, so foundation services come before applications. Loudness is not a priority criterion, restoring all at once ignores dependencies and capacity, and age says nothing about criticality.

questions.question: A storage administrator says the file server is protected because its disks are configured in RAID 5. Which risk does RAID 5 NOT address?
options: The failure of any single disk in the array
Accidental deletion or ransomware encryption of files
Reduced performance after one disk has failed in the array
The need to replace the failed disk without losing the array
questions.explanation: RAID protects against disk failure, but changes to data such as deletion or encryption are written across the array as normal. A single disk failure is what RAID 5 tolerates, and degraded operation and disk replacement are normal parts of how it works.

questions.question: The security team writes a document listing, for a suspected phishing compromise, the decision points, the actions for each role and who must be contacted. What is this document?
options: An incident response playbook for phishing
A configuration baseline for user laptops
A recovery point objective for the mail system
A legal hold notice sent to the mail administrators
questions.explanation: A playbook describes scenario-specific steps, decisions and roles. An RPO is a data loss target, a baseline records secure system configuration, and a legal hold instructs people to preserve data.

questions.question: A fire alarm sounds in the office. Which plan is MOST directly responsible for protecting the people in the building?
options: The occupant emergency plan
The configuration management plan
The risk register review procedure
The disaster recovery plan for the data center
questions.explanation: The occupant emergency plan covers evacuation and life safety. The DRP restores IT systems afterwards, configuration management covers system settings, and the risk register is a tracking tool, not an emergency procedure.

questions.question: A company needs to resume customer orders within hours of losing its main site and wants the cheapest option that still meets this. Which interim processing choice is MOST suitable?
options: A reciprocal agreement with a competitor company that has promised help but has no spare capacity
A cloud recovery environment or warm site that can be activated within hours
A cold site with empty rack space that would take weeks to equip fully
A plan to rebuild the site from scratch once insurance has paid out
questions.explanation: A warm site or cloud recovery environment can be brought up within hours at lower cost than a hot site. A cold site takes far too long, a reciprocal agreement without capacity is unreliable, and rebuilding after an insurance payout takes far longer than the requirement.

questions.question: Responders arrive at a site with a laptop, a phone, a server and a USB stick, but there is only time to image one device that day. Which approach is BEST?
options: Triage by relevance and volatility, image the top item and secure the rest with custody records
Image the first device that was found, because order of discovery decides priority
Power off all of the devices to stop changes, then image whichever one is easiest
Take nothing at all today, because collecting only part of the available evidence makes all of it inadmissible
questions.explanation: Triage prioritizes the evidence most relevant and most at risk, and everything else is secured with custody documentation. Discovery order is arbitrary, partial collection is acceptable when documented, and powering everything off destroys volatile data.

questions.question: Which TWO actions fit a first responder's duties at a suspected computer crime scene? (Choose two.)
options: Browse the files on the suspect computer to see what is on it
Keep unauthorized people away from the equipment
Plug in a personal USB drive to copy interesting files
Reboot the machine to check that it still works
Record the scene with photographs and written notes
questions.explanation: Documenting and securing the scene preserve evidence. Browsing files, connecting personal media and rebooting all alter the evidence.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about RAID and backups are correct? (Choose two.)
options: RAID 0 mirrors every disk, so it survives any disk failure
RAID keeps a system running through certain disk failures but does not protect against deletion or ransomware
Backups are unnecessary once a RAID array is installed
A backup should be stored where an attack on the production array cannot reach it
A RAID 5 array is a replacement for offline backups
questions.explanation: RAID is about availability against disk failure, and backups protect against data loss and must be isolated from the system they protect. RAID 0 stripes with no redundancy, and RAID does not replace backups.

questions.question: Which TWO items belong in a forensic report? (Choose two.)
options: Speculation presented as established fact
Only the findings that support the client's case
The limitations of the analysis and any contrary findings
Passwords that the examiner found on the system
The methods and tools used, with their versions
questions.explanation: A credible report lets others repeat the work and states limits and contrary evidence honestly. Selecting only favourable findings, presenting speculation as fact and listing found passwords undermine impartiality and confidentiality.

questions.question: In a criminal case the prosecution must prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt, which is a higher standard than the preponderance of evidence used in most civil cases.
questions.explanation: The criminal standard is the highest because liberty is at stake. Civil cases are decided on which side's version is more likely than not.

questions.question: A RAID 5 array is a sufficient substitute for backups.
questions.explanation: RAID tolerates disk failure, but deleted, corrupted or encrypted data is written to every disk, and the array shares the site with the original. Backups are needed too.

questions.question: A first responder who finds a running suspect computer should shut it down immediately by pulling the power.
questions.explanation: Volatile evidence such as memory and network connections would be lost. The responder records the state and follows the plan for isolation and hand-off.

questions.question: ISO/IEC 27035 includes a learn lessons phase so that findings improve later preparation.
questions.explanation: Like the NIST lifecycle, ISO/IEC 27035 ends with a review whose results feed back into preparation.

questions.question: An occupant emergency plan is mainly about restoring IT systems after a disaster.
questions.explanation: That describes a disaster recovery plan. The occupant emergency plan covers the safe evacuation and protection of people.

questions.question: A retailer's checkout application stores the card number and the three-digit security code of each customer in an encrypted database so that returning customers can pay faster. What is the main problem under PCI DSS?
options: The security code is sensitive authentication data and may not be kept after authorization
The database should use a faster algorithm because encrypted storage slows checkout down
The database must be hashed with MD5 instead of being encrypted, so that nobody can read it
The card number counts as public information and does not need to be rendered unreadable
questions.explanation: Verification codes, full track data and PINs may not be retained after authorization, regardless of encryption. The speed of the algorithm is not the issue, a stored card number must be unreadable, and MD5 is a broken hash that would not support the payment use anyway.

questions.question: Several virtual machines were cloned from one template. A review shows they all generated identical SSH host keys on first boot. What is the MOST likely root cause?
options: Insufficient entropy or an identical random state when the keys were generated
The virtual machines used a hash function instead of a symmetric cipher when generating their host identities
The SSH protocol cannot produce unique keys under any circumstances
The administrator chose a key length that was too short for the cipher
questions.explanation: Keys generated from the same random state, with no fresh entropy, come out identical. SSH can create unique keys, hashing versus encryption does not explain duplicate values, and key length would not make different machines produce the same key.

questions.question: An agency wants to protect long-lived data against a future quantum computer while using its existing servers and network equipment. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
options: Rely on 1024-bit RSA because quantum computers cannot factor numbers that small
Plan migration to NIST-standardized post-quantum algorithms such as ML-KEM and ML-DSA
Switch from AES-256 to AES-128 because shorter keys are quantum resistant
Deploy quantum key distribution links across every branch office and cloud region as the only protection
questions.explanation: Post-quantum algorithms run on conventional hardware and are standardized by NIST. QKD needs special hardware and distance-limited links and does not fit this requirement, shorter AES keys would reduce strength, and 1024-bit RSA is weak long before quantum computers matter.

questions.question: Which statement about a large quantum computer is correct?
options: Grover's algorithm breaks AES-256 as quickly as it would break AES-128
Shor's algorithm makes every cryptographic hash function instantly reversible by anyone
Quantum computers make symmetric cryptography useless in exactly the same way as RSA
Shor's algorithm threatens RSA and elliptic-curve keys, while AES-256 remains strong
questions.explanation: Shor's algorithm breaks the number-theoretic problems behind RSA, Diffie-Hellman and ECC. Grover's algorithm only roughly halves symmetric strength, so AES-256 keeps adequate strength, hashes are not made reversible, and symmetric cryptography survives with larger keys.

questions.question: A company is choosing an elliptic-curve key size that gives security strength comparable to RSA-3072. Which is the BEST match?
options: A 2048-bit elliptic curve key, to match common RSA keys
A 256-bit elliptic curve key
A 112-bit elliptic curve key
A 3072-bit elliptic curve key, to match the RSA size
questions.explanation: Elliptic-curve keys are much smaller for the same strength, and 256-bit curves offer about 128 bits of security like RSA-3072. A 112-bit curve is too weak, and matching raw bit counts to RSA misunderstands how the algorithms scale.

questions.question: A cryptanalyst has a set of captured messages together with the original text of a few of them and attempts to work out the key. Which attack setting is this?
options: Chosen-plaintext attack, because the analyst selected which messages to read
Known-plaintext attack
Ciphertext-only attack, because ciphertext is available to the analyst
Birthday attack, because several messages are being compared with each other
questions.explanation: Having plaintext matched with its ciphertext is a known-plaintext setting. Ciphertext-only means no plaintext is known, chosen-plaintext requires that the attacker can pick plaintexts for the system to encrypt, and a birthday attack looks for hash collisions.

questions.question: Two systems perform an unauthenticated Diffie-Hellman key exchange over an untrusted network. Which risk remains?
options: Both systems are guaranteed to derive different keys and cannot communicate
The exchange cannot provide forward secrecy under any possible configuration
A man-in-the-middle can run separate exchanges with each side and read the traffic
The shared secret must be sent in cleartext to the other party for it to be agreed
questions.explanation: Without authentication, neither side knows who it is talking to, so an interceptor can run separate exchanges with each. The secret is never sent, ephemeral variants give forward secrecy, and both sides do derive the same key.

questions.question: A small group of researchers wants to exchange encrypted email without relying on a commercial certificate authority. Which approach fits best, and how do they establish trust in each other's keys?
options: A single shared passphrase that every person types into each message they send
Unencrypted email, relying on link-level encryption between the participants' mail servers
OpenPGP or GnuPG, with keys checked by fingerprint and signed by trusted members
S/MIME, with certificates issued by a public certificate authority that the group avoids
questions.explanation: OpenPGP uses a web of trust in which users verify and sign one another's keys. S/MIME depends on a CA, which they want to avoid, a shared passphrase scales badly and cannot prove who sent a message, and transport encryption does not protect messages end to end.

questions.question: A company wants centrally managed signing and encryption of email, with certificates issued, renewed and revoked by an internal authority. Which technology fits BEST?
options: A VPN between the mail server and each employee device
PGP with a web of trust maintained by each employee individually
SPF records published in the company's DNS zone
S/MIME with certificates from the company's PKI
questions.explanation: S/MIME uses X.509 certificates managed by a CA, which fits central control. A web of trust is decentralized and hard to manage, SPF authorizes sending servers rather than signing messages, and a VPN protects a connection, not the message.

questions.question: Employees' laptops use full-disk encryption. One employee forgets the passphrase and the business needs the data. Which design would have allowed legitimate recovery?
options: A key escrow or recovery arrangement with dual control and an audit trail
Storing every user's passphrase in a shared spreadsheet on the file server
Disabling encryption on all laptops so no recovery is ever needed
Asking the employee to guess at the passphrase until it works
questions.explanation: Escrow gives an authorized recovery path while limiting who can use it. A shared spreadsheet exposes every passphrase, disabling encryption removes the protection and guessing is neither reliable nor safe.

questions.question: A certificate authority is found to have issued a valid certificate for the company's domain to an unknown party. Which control would have detected this MOST directly?
options: Enabling split tunnelling on the corporate VPN for all remote workers
Turning on full-disk encryption for every company laptop
Monitoring certificate transparency logs for certificates issued to the company domain
Raising the minimum length of all employee passwords and requiring a change every thirty days across the company
questions.explanation: Certificate transparency logs publicly record issued certificates, so monitoring them reveals unexpected ones. Password length, split tunnelling and disk encryption do not detect misissued certificates.

questions.question: An e-commerce site needs to protect card data entered by customers and stored for recurring billing. Which combination is MOST appropriate?
options: Hashing the card number with MD5 in transit and leaving the stored copy clear, so that the database is easy to search
TLS in transit, and tokenization or strong encryption for the stored card number
Encoding the card number with Base64 for storage and sending it over plain HTTP, because encoding hides it
Relying on the customer's browser to encrypt the number before it is stored
questions.explanation: Different data states need different controls: TLS in transit, and tokenization or strong encryption at rest. Base64 is an encoding and not protection, MD5 is a broken hash and not suited to this, and browser behaviour cannot protect stored data.

questions.question: Which TWO are recognized limitations or vulnerabilities of public key infrastructure? (Choose two.)
options: A public key must be kept secret to remain secure
Revocation information may not be checked or may be slow to reach clients
Certificates make encryption of data in transit impossible
A compromised or careless certificate authority can issue fraudulent certificates
PKI removes the need to protect private keys
questions.explanation: PKI inherits trust from CAs and depends on timely revocation checking. Certificates enable encryption, public keys are meant to be shared, and private keys still need strong protection.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about quantum key distribution (QKD) are correct? (Choose two.)
options: It runs on ordinary servers and requires no special equipment
It still needs an authenticated classical channel and special hardware
It distributes keys, and an eavesdropper disturbs the quantum states in a detectable way
It is the same thing as post-quantum cryptography
It encrypts bulk data directly without any use of symmetric keys
questions.explanation: QKD agrees keys using quantum effects and detects interception, but needs authentication and dedicated links. It does not encrypt bulk data directly, it needs special equipment, and post-quantum cryptography is classical mathematics, which is a different approach.

questions.question: Which TWO practices improve password storage? (Choose two.)
options: Store passwords with reversible encryption using one key in the same database
Use a slow password hashing function such as Argon2 or bcrypt
Use a unique random salt for every password hash
Hash with a single round of MD5 for speed
Use one global salt shared by every user
questions.explanation: Unique salts and slow hashing make precomputation and mass guessing impractical. Reversible encryption next to its key, shared salts and MD5 are all weak.

questions.question: Quantum key distribution transmits the message itself securely using quantum particles.
questions.explanation: QKD establishes a shared key. The message is then protected by conventional encryption using that key.

questions.question: Post-quantum cryptography requires the use of a quantum computer to run.
questions.explanation: Post-quantum algorithms are classical mathematics that run on ordinary computers while resisting known quantum attacks.

questions.question: Doubling the key length always makes an encryption scheme stronger, even if the algorithm itself is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken or weak algorithm cannot be rescued by a longer key. Strength depends on both the algorithm and the key.

questions.question: In a web of trust there is a single central root certificate authority that every user must trust.
questions.explanation: A web of trust is decentralized: users sign one another's keys and decide whom to trust. A central root CA belongs to hierarchical PKI.

questions.question: Under PCI DSS the card verification code may be stored after authorization if it is encrypted.
questions.explanation: Sensitive authentication data must not be stored after authorization, even when encrypted.

questions.question: Triple DES (3DES) is a recommended modern choice for new systems.
questions.explanation: 3DES has a small block size and is retired by NIST for encryption. AES is the standard for new systems.

questions.question: A small office uses a star topology with every workstation connected to a single switch. A technician asks which risk is MOST important to address. What is it?
options: Traffic must circulate in one direction, so a break anywhere stops the network
All workstations share one cable that limits the data rate for everyone
Each workstation can be taken offline by removing any other workstation's cable
The central switch is a single point of failure for every connected workstation
questions.explanation: In a star, every node depends on the central device, so its failure isolates all of them. Failure of one node's cable affects only that node, and the descriptions of one-way circulation and one shared cable apply to ring and bus designs.

questions.question: A company plans a full mesh between six sites, with a direct link between every pair of sites. How many links are needed?
questions.explanation: A full mesh of n nodes needs n(n-1)/2 links, which is 6 times 5 divided by 2, or 15. Six would be a ring, twelve is a mistaken count of two links per site, and thirty counts each link twice.

questions.question: A network administrator splits a network using a /26 prefix. How many usable host addresses does each subnet provide?
questions.explanation: A /26 leaves 6 host bits, giving 64 addresses, and two of them are the network and broadcast addresses, so 62 are usable. Sixty-four forgets the reserved addresses, 30 matches a /27 and 126 matches a /25.

questions.question: A factory floor has heavy electrical machinery that causes interference, and data must cross 400 metres between two buildings. Which cabling is MOST appropriate?
options: Unshielded twisted-pair copper cable
Coaxial cable run next to the power lines
Fiber optic cable
A long Ethernet patch lead chained through several couplers
questions.explanation: Fiber is immune to electromagnetic interference and easily covers long distances. Twisted pair is limited to about 100 metres and picks up interference, and the other two options add interference or exceed distance limits.

questions.question: The security team must allow administrators to manage Linux servers remotely using only an encrypted protocol. Which firewall rule is MOST appropriate?
options: Allow TCP port 22 from the management subnet
Allow TCP port 21 from the management subnet
Allow TCP port 23 from any address on the internet
Allow UDP port 69 from any address on the internet
questions.explanation: Port 22 is SSH, which encrypts the session, and limiting it to the management subnet narrows exposure. Port 23 is cleartext Telnet, port 21 is cleartext FTP control and UDP 69 is TFTP, which has no authentication.

questions.question: In a software-defined network, which component makes the forwarding decisions for the switches and is therefore the highest-value target for an attacker?
options: An individual access port on one edge switch
The central controller
The patch cable between two switches
A user's workstation network card
questions.explanation: The controller holds the control plane and programs every device, so compromising it can reconfigure the whole network. A single port, cable or network card affects far less.

questions.question: A retailer wants its branch stores to use a mix of broadband and cellular links, with central policy, application-aware routing and encrypted tunnels. Which technology is designed for this?
options: Dial-up connections with a modem pool
SD-WAN
A single leased line per store with static routes
A hub-and-spoke frame relay circuit
questions.explanation: SD-WAN manages several transports centrally and steers applications by policy. Frame relay and single leased lines are fixed and costly, and dial-up is obsolete and slow.

questions.question: Users who type the correct bank address are sent to a convincing fake site, and the issue disappears when they use a different resolver. What is the MOST likely attack?
options: A rogue DHCP server handing out the wrong subnet mask
A cross-site scripting flaw in the bank's login page
A SYN flood against the bank's web server
DNS cache poisoning on the first resolver
questions.explanation: Forged records in a resolver's cache send users to attacker addresses, and a different resolver gives correct answers. A SYN flood causes outages and does not redirect users, a wrong subnet mask breaks connectivity, and cross-site scripting runs in the page rather than changing name resolution.

questions.question: A victim's link is saturated by large DNS replies they never asked for, sent from thousands of legitimate servers. Which attack and defence BEST match?
options: ARP spoofing on the victim's local network, countered by dynamic ARP inspection and DHCP snooping on its switches
VLAN hopping, countered by changing the native VLAN on the trunk
Password spraying, countered by account lockout thresholds
Reflection and amplification, countered by ingress and egress filtering and closing open resolvers
questions.explanation: Spoofed small queries trigger large replies that go to the victim, and filtering and closing open resolvers limit abuse. ARP spoofing, VLAN hopping and password spraying involve other layers and techniques.

questions.question: A news site serves large amounts of static content and is hit by high-volume floods. Which control MOST directly helps absorb the traffic?
options: A longer password policy for the site administrators
A content delivery network with DDoS protection
Full-disk encryption on the origin web servers
A second login page for the administration area
questions.explanation: A CDN spreads traffic across many edge locations and filters volumetric attacks upstream. Password policy, disk encryption and extra login pages do nothing to absorb floods.

questions.question: Contractors use their own unmanaged laptops, and the company wants to ensure that no corporate data is stored on those devices. Which approach BEST meets this?
options: Virtual desktops with clipboard, drive and print redirection disabled
A written policy that asks contractors to delete any corporate files from their laptops when they finish
Emailing documents to the contractors' personal accounts
A VPN with split tunnelling and file shares mapped locally
questions.explanation: In virtual desktop infrastructure, the data stays in the data center and redirection can be blocked. A VPN with local file shares puts data on the device, a policy relies on goodwill, and personal email loses control.

questions.question: A server's remote desktop port is open to the internet and shows thousands of failed sign-ins each day. What is the BEST remediation?
options: Hide the server's host name from public DNS and keep the port open, but add a banner that warns attackers off
Increase the number of failed attempts allowed before lockout
Remove the public exposure and require access through a VPN or gateway with MFA
Change the port number from 3389 to a less common value only
questions.explanation: Exposed remote desktop is a top ransomware vector, so remove it from the internet and require strong authentication through a gateway. Changing the port number and hiding the name are obscurity, and allowing more attempts helps the attacker.

questions.question: A network team wants to keep administering routers when the production network is down or compromised. Which design supports this BEST?
options: SNMP version 2c with the default community string
Administration over the production VLAN using Telnet from any workstation
An out-of-band management network reached through a hardened jump host
Shared administrator credentials printed on each device
questions.explanation: A separate management path stays reachable and limits who can reach management interfaces. Telnet over the production network, printed shared credentials and SNMP v2c with a default string are insecure and fail when the network fails.

questions.question: A router receives a packet and consults its table to send it out of the correct interface. Which plane performs this forwarding?
options: The management plane, which administrators use to configure the device
The application plane, which holds the web interface of the device
The data plane
The control plane, which also builds the routing table from routing protocols
questions.explanation: The data plane forwards packets. The control plane builds the tables the data plane uses, and the management plane is the administrative access path. There is no separate application plane in this model.

questions.question: An ICS network controls a water treatment process and must never be reachable from the corporate network or the internet. Which design gives the strongest separation?
options: A wireless bridge between the plant and the office with a shared passphrase that is changed every month
A VLAN on the corporate switch with the same router as the office network
A firewall rule that allows all traffic from the corporate subnet to the plant and logs every connection it sees
Physical segmentation, such as an air gap, with controlled one-way data transfer where needed
questions.explanation: Physical separation removes the connection, and controlled data transfer limits what crosses. A VLAN on shared equipment, a permissive firewall rule and a wireless bridge all leave a path an attacker can use.

questions.question: A legacy web application has an SQL injection flaw that cannot be fixed for several weeks. Which interim control is MOST appropriate?
options: Rely on the existing stateful network firewall to block the injection requests, since it already sees all web traffic
Hide the application's login URL from search engines
Add web application firewall rules for injection as a virtual patch, and schedule the code fix
Disable the server's logging so the attacks are not recorded
questions.explanation: A WAF can virtually patch by inspecting HTTP requests while the code fix is prepared. A network firewall does not read web request content, disabling logging removes detection and hiding the URL is obscurity.

questions.question: Voice calls between offices become choppy whenever nightly backups run over the same WAN link. Which control BEST addresses this?
options: Compressing the voice calls with the same tool used for backups
Switching the voice calls to a protocol with no encryption at all
Running the backups at the same time as the busiest call period
Quality of service rules that prioritize voice traffic over backup traffic
questions.explanation: Traffic shaping and QoS give latency-sensitive traffic priority. Compressing voice with backup tools does not set priority, turning off encryption does not solve congestion, and running backups at peak call time makes it worse.

questions.question: An executive's phone connects to a rogue cellular base station in a hotel lobby that forces a weaker connection. What is the BEST protection for the content of the communication?
options: Using SMS rather than data to send sensitive messages
Trusting the carrier's radio encryption alone, because the carrier says that it protects the full path of the call
End-to-end encryption or a VPN, because the cellular path cannot be trusted for confidentiality
Disabling the phone's screen lock to speed up reconnection
questions.explanation: A fake base station can sit in the path, so confidentiality must come from encryption applied above the cellular link. The radio encryption does not cover the whole path, a disabled screen lock reduces security and SMS is interceptable.

questions.question: An attacker within a few metres of a visitor's phone uses a Bluetooth weakness to copy the visitor's contact list without any pairing prompt. Which attack is this?
options: Bluesnarfing
War driving, where wireless networks are mapped from a vehicle
Evil twin, where an access point impersonates the corporate SSID
Bluejacking, where unsolicited messages are pushed to nearby devices
questions.explanation: Unauthorized data theft over Bluetooth is bluesnarfing. Bluejacking sends unwanted messages, war driving surveys networks and an evil twin impersonates a Wi-Fi access point.

questions.question: A company wants the strongest wireless authentication for staff laptops and is prepared to run a PKI. Which EAP method fits BEST?
options: EAP-TLS using certificates on the server and each client
LEAP using a shared password hash
A pre-shared key printed on posters in the office
An open network with a captive portal for each user
questions.explanation: EAP-TLS authenticates both sides with certificates and has no reusable password to steal. LEAP is obsolete and weak, a pre-shared key cannot identify people and a captive portal on an open network does not encrypt traffic.

questions.question: A site has ten IP cameras that run old firmware with default passwords, and the vendor has stopped issuing updates. What is the BEST approach?
options: Isolate them on their own segment, change credentials where possible and plan to replace them
Leave them on the office network as they are, because cameras do not hold sensitive data and nobody attacks them
Install antivirus software on each camera to protect the old firmware
Expose them to the internet so that staff can watch them remotely
questions.explanation: Unsupported devices are isolated with limited traffic while replacement is planned. Leaving them on the main network creates a pivot point for attackers, cameras cannot usually run antivirus, and exposing them online invites compromise.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about software-defined networking are correct? (Choose two.)
options: The controller must be protected because it can change policy for many devices
SDN controllers need no authentication because they are internal
The control plane is separated from the data plane and managed centrally
SDN removes the need for network segmentation
SDN means every switch makes its own independent forwarding decisions
questions.explanation: SDN centralizes control and therefore concentrates risk in the controller. It enables, not removes, segmentation, switches follow the controller's programming and controllers need strong authentication.

questions.question: Which TWO controls help protect the management plane of network devices? (Choose two.)
options: Share one administrative password among all engineers
Use SSH with centralized AAA and individual accounts
Administer through a dedicated management network or out-of-band path
Allow Telnet from any internal subnet for convenience
Use the vendor default community string for SNMP
questions.explanation: A separate management path and individual, authenticated, logged access limit who can reconfigure devices. Telnet, default SNMP strings and shared passwords all weaken the plane.

questions.question: Which TWO are sound ways to secure Internet of Things devices? (Choose two.)
options: Ignore end-of-life dates because the devices still work
Connect them directly to the internet so that the vendor can reach them
Choose devices with signed updates and a published support period
Leave default credentials in place so support staff can always log in
Place them on a separate network segment with limited allowed traffic
questions.explanation: Isolation and supportable devices reduce exposure. Default credentials, direct internet exposure and unsupported devices create persistent vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Which TWO are correct statements about wireless security? (Choose two.)
options: WPA3 uses Simultaneous Authentication of Equals to resist offline password guessing
EAP-TLS authenticates both the server and the client with certificates
Hiding the SSID is a reliable way to secure an access point
PEAP does not need a server certificate to be validated by clients
WEP remains acceptable if the key is changed every day
questions.explanation: SAE and mutual certificate authentication are strengths of WPA3 and EAP-TLS. WEP is broken whatever the key, hidden SSIDs are easy to discover, and clients must validate the server certificate for PEAP to be safe.

questions.question: Which TWO attacks can be mitigated mainly by DNSSEC validation, randomized source ports and restricting recursion? (Choose two.)
options: ARP spoofing on a local switch
Cross-site scripting in web forms
SYN floods against web servers
DNS cache poisoning
Forged DNS responses that redirect users to attacker servers
questions.explanation: These controls address forged or poisoned DNS data. SYN floods, ARP spoofing and cross-site scripting are different attacks that need different defences.

questions.question: In a full mesh of n nodes, every pair of nodes has its own direct link, giving n(n-1)/2 links.
questions.explanation: The count grows quickly with each added node, which is why full meshes are rare except for small, critical sets of nodes.

questions.question: A /24 network has 254 usable host addresses.
questions.explanation: A /24 has 256 addresses, and the network and broadcast addresses are not assigned to hosts.

questions.question: SDN gives every switch its own independent control plane that is configured by hand.
questions.explanation: SDN separates and centralizes the control plane in a controller, which programs the data plane devices.

questions.question: A web application firewall protects web applications by inspecting HTTP traffic and can block patterns such as SQL injection.
questions.explanation: It works at the application layer, which ordinary packet-filtering firewalls do not inspect. It supplements, rather than replaces, secure code.

questions.question: NFC is a long-range technology, so eavesdropping on it is possible only from several hundred metres away.
questions.explanation: NFC works over a few centimetres. Eavesdropping needs close proximity, though relay attacks can extend the effective distance.

questions.question: Bluesnarfing is the unauthorized theft of data from a Bluetooth device.
questions.explanation: Bluejacking sends unsolicited messages and bluebugging takes control, while bluesnarfing steals information.

questions.question: Cellular encryption between the phone and the carrier means that data is protected end to end across the internet.
questions.explanation: The radio link is encrypted, but protection beyond the carrier's network needs end-to-end encryption or a VPN.

questions.question: An out-of-band management network lets administrators reach network devices even when the production network is unavailable.
questions.explanation: The separate path stays up independently and can be tightly controlled with a jump host, MFA and logging.

questions.question: A technician finds that security tools on a server report nothing, yet the machine behaves oddly and network traffic shows connections to an unknown address. A scan run from a rescue disk reveals a hidden driver. What does this MOST likely indicate?
options: A logic bomb that has not yet reached the date on which it is set to run but is already making connections
A macro virus that has infected only documents stored on one file share
A rootkit that hides itself from tools running inside the compromised operating system
A scareware program that is displaying pop-up warnings to scare the user
questions.explanation: Hidden components that only show up when the system is examined from outside are typical of a rootkit, which tampers with what the running operating system reports. Scareware is visible by design, a macro virus lives in documents and a dormant logic bomb would not be making network connections.

questions.question: A free screen-saver program installs normally, then quietly opens a hidden remote connection for an attacker. How is this program BEST classified?
options: A trojan, because it hides a harmful function inside software that looks useful
A trapdoor, because it was written by the developers of the operating system
A worm, because it opened a connection over the network to another system
A boot-sector virus, because it was installed and runs after the system starts
questions.explanation: A trojan looks legitimate while carrying a hidden function, and does not replicate itself. A worm copies itself across networks on its own, a boot-sector virus infects the startup area, and a trapdoor is an undocumented entry left by a developer in their own code.

questions.question: Within minutes of one unpatched server being turned on, copies of the same program appear on dozens of other unpatched servers with no user action at all. Which malware behaviour is this?
options: Scareware that scares staff into passing on a warning email
A trojan that needs each user to choose to install it
Worm propagation through a network service vulnerability
A macro virus spreading when users open shared documents
questions.explanation: Self-replication across the network by exploiting a vulnerable service, without any user action, is a worm. Macro viruses and trojans rely on users opening or installing something, and scareware spreads through persuasion, not exploitation.

questions.question: A developer checks that a file is safe to open and then opens it, but an attacker swaps the file in the short gap between the two steps. Which weakness is this?
options: A race condition of the time of check to time of use type
A buffer overflow caused by missing bounds checking of the input
SQL injection caused by concatenating text into a database query
Cross-site scripting caused by unencoded output in a web page
questions.explanation: When the state changes between a check and the later use, the result is a race condition, specifically time of check to time of use. A buffer overflow writes past a memory boundary, and the injection and scripting flaws involve untrusted input interpreted as commands or markup.

questions.question: A web page the staff routinely read for industry news is compromised and silently installs malware on visitors' laptops. Which attack is this?
options: A distributed denial of service attack against the publisher
A watering-hole attack that uses a drive-by download
A smishing campaign sent by text message to company phones
A spear-phishing campaign that targets a single named executive
questions.explanation: Compromising a site that a target group is known to visit, so that visitors are infected, is a watering-hole attack, and the silent install is a drive-by download. Phishing and smishing deliver lures by email or text, and a denial of service aims to make the site unavailable.

questions.question: An attacker's page makes a logged-in user's browser send a request to the bank's transfer function without the user noticing. Which defence is MOST effective against this?
options: Parameterized queries in the database layer behind the transfer function
Anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies on the application's sensitive requests
Full-disk encryption on the bank's application servers
A longer minimum password length for all of the bank's customers
questions.explanation: A forged cross-site request succeeds because the browser attaches the session automatically, so unpredictable per-request tokens and SameSite cookies block it. Parameterized queries stop injection, password length does not affect an authenticated session, and disk encryption protects data at rest.

questions.question: A finance manager receives a text message that appears to come from the bank, stating that the account will be frozen unless a link is opened within an hour. What is this attack, and what is the BEST response?
options: Vishing; call back the number shown in the message to check it quickly
Spam; ignore it, because unwanted bulk messages are not harmful
Whaling; reply to the sender to confirm that the account is genuine
Smishing; do not use the link and contact the bank through a known number
questions.explanation: A text-message lure is smishing, and the urgency is a pressure tactic, so the safe move is to use an independently known contact route. Vishing uses voice calls, replying or calling back through the supplied details stays inside the attacker's channel, and treating it as harmless spam ignores the credential-theft risk.

questions.question: An analyst reviews a user account that normally downloads a few files a day but has just copied 40 GB from the engineering share at 3 a.m. from a new location. Which type of tool is MOST likely to flag this automatically?
options: A signature-based antivirus scanner on the user's laptop
A hardware security module in the data center
User and entity behaviour analytics that compares activity with a baseline
A static application security testing tool in the build pipeline
questions.explanation: Behaviour analytics learns what is normal for each user and raises alerts on deviations such as unusual volume, time and place. An antivirus scanner looks for known malware, an HSM protects keys and a static testing tool inspects source code before release.

questions.question: A company cannot patch a newly disclosed flaw in an internet-facing application for ten days because the vendor has not released a fix. What is the BEST interim step?
options: Tell users to avoid the application unless they feel that it is safe
Wait for the vendor to release the fix and take no other action meanwhile
Apply a virtual patch with an intrusion prevention system or web application firewall rule
